product_536.description:
General Information
A chair as it is written in the book
And that nothing can knock over so quickly. Its frame is made of solid beech wood, the seat is available either as a seat frame with woven cane or as a plywood panel with upholstery and cowhide covering.
Rabenau. The chairmaking town
Rabenau's chairmaking tradition is almost 400 years old. The many special skills of Rabenau's chairmakers that have grown over that time have survived industrialization, and they have survived the Volkseigentum and the Federal Republic's Vocational Training Ordinance unscathed. Today, 16 factories work under the umbrella of a cooperative. They manufacture chairs and tables in a manner committed to the best traditions of the trade. What the Rabenauer chairmakers can do, they show especially in the faithful reproduction of historical models.
The Nikolai furniture
In 1910, the Rabenauer supplied the following seating furniture and tables to equip the four hundred year old "Old Nikolai School" at the Nikolaikirchhof in Leipzig. For the reopening of the renovated building as a cultural center in 1994, the furniture was built a second time in Rabenau. For "private use" they are only available from us.
The processing
The frames and seat frames of the Rabenau furniture are made of solid beech wood, which is stained and varnished. The wood joints are tapped and cold glued. The seat frames of the seating furniture are mitered and the edges are profile milled; typical leg shape with rod milling.
The seats: Leather or wicker
The seating surfaces are either leather seats or wickerwork:
- The leather seats consist of a plywood base, which is padded with upholstery wadding; black cowhide is fixed on it with decorative nails.
- For the wickerwork seating surfaces, the split, stained peddigree is woven three times by hand through holes in the chair fold.
Restoration possible
In cooperation with the Rabenau chair makers, we offer to refurbish older models of chairs of this type. You will receive an offer on request, the duration of the restoration depends on the effort.

product_539.description:
General Information
As strong as an oak tree
By design, or even better, by workshop design, spindle stools are work furniture that fulfill a precisely defined purpose: to provide users with a flexible, adjustable seat height to give them an overview at work - at any table, for any height. The simple yet highly functional technical solution for this requirement is mechanical height adjustment via a threaded spindle. The formal design of such a stool also follows this purpose alone and is limited to the essentials: the frame inspired by the three-legged stool, a spindle, a seat - minimalism at its best. This example shows how the original workshop furniture can be transformed into an impressive, ultra-modern piece of home furniture with added interior design value: the spindle stool is made entirely from solid local oak, right down to its central element.
A spindle made of oak wood may come as a surprise at first, but oak wood is famous for being extremely hard, tough and durable. Even under water, it resists rotting for centuries. In short, not only many people and animals, but also this stool and its spindle are "strong as an oak", reliably lifting its user up and back down again and also conquering additional areas of use: Because thanks to the completely flat seat surface, it holds its own just as solidly as an adaptable side table. Whether you use it as a flexible seat or as a stable storage surface: The opulence of the material in the stool contrasts with the simplicity of the design in a visually exciting way, which fulfills its interior design function with lasting stability. Once you have chosen it, you won't be able to get rid of this spindle stool in a hurry. A handcrafted heirloom that moves between the poles of elegant restraint and strong character, proving its modernity over time.
Tradition x modernity. Mint Furniture
Anyone who still thinks that traditional craftsmanship results in furniture à la Gelsenkirchen Baroque should turn their gaze to Riga. There, the company Mint Furniture, founded in 2009, stands for furniture design in which the tried and tested is taken up and further developed in form and function. This is the essence of innovation anyway, especially when it wants to stand out from the mass of supposed modernity in a visionary way. The team at Mint Furniture, which combines knowledge of fine art, interior design, industrial design and craftsmanship, has also achieved something astonishing: an individual design signature that is revealed in the fine details. With his spindle stool made of solid oak, co-founder Janis Rauza laid the foundation for the creative combination of formal tradition and functional modernity. Continuously expanded, the entire furniture collection from Mint Furniture follows this vision: expertly crafted by cabinetmakers, supported by a profound knowledge of the possibilities of the material and supported by the use of modern technologies, the designs point far into the future as pieces for generations.

General Information
The INOX shelving system was developed as a storage system for sterile goods and sterile clothing and is used as such in laboratories and other sterile rooms. These mesh baskets, which are part of the system, offer plenty of space for all kinds of storage items and can be hooked into the associated wall rails without tools. Whether towels in the bathroom, crockery in the kitchen or scarves and cycle helmets in the checkroom: the mesh baskets provide a well-ventilated and visible place for everything. The baskets are made of high-quality, electrolytically polished stainless steel round material from the medical sector, are virtually indestructible and easy to clean. product_553.description:
General Information
Discover MAGAZIN products: Collaborating with innovative designers, MAGAZIN develops and produces this unique furniture and home accessories series.
The wall bracket for the CONTAINER DS in its classic size and the shelf element TARA. It turns the container into a cabinet on the wall: to be mounted at different heights, free-floating individually or in plural as a sideboard, as a wall unit in the kitchen, in hallways as a shoe cabinet and for the utensils of everyday life, as well as for many other purposes. The screws and dowels needed for mounting are included.
Series Container DS
Synonymous with storage and transport: the container in its archetypal surface of folded steel. We offer this cabinet furniture in the miniaturized form of overseas containers in four different versions. These well-proportioned storage boxes serve many purposes and areas of use. All containers have perforations in the bottoms for passing cables. The classic container as well as the flat and small container have doors hinged to the top of the body, which slide into the top of the body when opened and thus almost completely disappear. The CONTAINER DS PLUS is upright and has a conventional hinged door on the side.
The classic: The CONTAINER DS in the proportion of a sea container is virtually the archetype of the series CONTAINER DS. It serves as a cabinet in the living room for china and utensils for the set table, in the office for storing files in standardized format or for paper and office utensils. As a chest of drawers for linen and as a piece of furniture in the hallway and wardrobe. It can be combined in its basic rectangular shape with a variety of complementary accessories. Various feet and casters or the two framework frames serve as the basis. The shelf element TARA has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery. The coat rack completes the container to a functional wardrobe. The container of this format is available in limited color selection equipped with a lock. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The flat one: CONTAINER DS FLAT has the footprint of the classic CONTAINER DS and can be connected to it in height and stacked. It can be combined with the above mentioned accessories of the classic CONTAINER DS. This container often serves as a flat element that is built into a stack of the classic container. It is useful with its special volume for the stack of paper, for utensils and as a shelf for many purposes. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The small one: The CONTAINER DS KLEIN as the little brother of the CONTAINER DS does not have the proportions of a sea container, unlike its archetypal big role model - it is narrower, with identical depth and height. With its small size and unusual formatting, it serves as a piece of side furniture next to the bed and sofa and can also be stacked up to form a tower. It can be equipped with all separate feet as well as the casters. Unlike its sister models, it is always equipped with a smooth cover shelf in the respective color. The shelf element TARA KLEIN has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery.
The big one: A very special piece of furniture with its own range of uses is the CONTAINER DS PLUS. It can be used in portrait format and serves as a locker-like clothes or wardrobe cabinet and can also be used as a large-volume cabinet, individually or stacked on top of each other in the kitchen, office or other places. This large container is stackable like all other sister models via included square connectors. A clothes rail is included, and a specially designed shelf and cover shelf are available separately as accessories.

product_567.description:
General Information
The INOX shelving system was developed as a storage system for sterile goods and sterile clothing and is used as such in laboratories and other sterile rooms. Medical staff hang their shoes on this hook rail for the INOX shelving system after work. We quickly repurpose them and bring them, together with wall rails and other accessories, into the living area as storage furniture. They can be hooked into the corresponding wall rails without tools and used as towel rails in the bathroom, as shoe or bag holders in the checkroom or as cooking utensil holders in the kitchen. Made of electrolytically polished and burr-free stainless steel wire, the hooks are virtually indestructible and easy to clean. Incidentally, the hook rail can also be screwed to the wall without the accompanying wall rails and used as a shoe rack. The fixing material required for this application is not included in the scope of delivery.
HUPFER - Münsterland efficiency
For 155 years, Hupfer Metallwerke from Coesfeld has been ensuring smooth processes in places where cleanliness is paramount. Founded in 1870 in Saxony-Anhalt as a wire mesh manufacturer, the company equips commercial kitchens, clinics and clean rooms for pharmaceutical companies with its systems. Furniture, trolleys, shelving systems, work surfaces, technology and accessories. With a high degree of specialization, virtually indestructible and ideally adapted to their tasks. The focus here is on special requirements: all Hupfer products must meet special hygiene specifications. This is achieved with a special steel that the company polishes electrolytically, making its surface infinitely durable. The design, in turn, ensures smooth, low-contact processes and high utility value. We have selected a wall hook rail from the medical sector from the wide range on offer, into which various accessories - baskets, hook rails, shelves, etc. - can be hung, and which can thus be combined to create individual storage furniture.

product_568.description:
General Information
A chair as it is written in the book
And that nothing can knock over so quickly. Its frame is made of solid beech wood, the seat is available either as a seat frame with woven cane or as a plywood panel with upholstery and cowhide covering.
Rabenau. The chairmaking town
Rabenau's chairmaking tradition is almost 400 years old. The many special skills of Rabenau's chairmakers that have grown over that time have survived industrialization, and they have survived the Volkseigentum and the Federal Republic's Vocational Training Ordinance unscathed. Today, 16 factories work under the umbrella of a cooperative. They manufacture chairs and tables in a manner committed to the best traditions of the trade. What the Rabenauer chairmakers can do, they show especially in the faithful reproduction of historical models.
The Nikolai furniture
In 1910, the Rabenauer supplied the following seating furniture and tables to equip the four hundred year old "Old Nikolai School" at the Nikolaikirchhof in Leipzig. For the reopening of the renovated building as a cultural center in 1994, the furniture was built a second time in Rabenau. For "private use" they are only available from us.
The processing
The frames and seat frames of the Rabenau furniture are made of solid beech wood, which is stained and varnished. The wood joints are tapped and cold glued. The seat frames of the seating furniture are mitered and the edges are profile milled; typical leg shape with rod milling.
The seats: Leather or wicker
The seating surfaces are either leather seats or wickerwork:
- The leather seats consist of a plywood base, which is padded with upholstery wadding; black cowhide is fixed on it with decorative nails.
- For the wickerwork seating surfaces, the split, stained peddigree is woven three times by hand through holes in the chair fold.
Restoration possible
In cooperation with the Rabenau chair makers, we offer to refurbish older models of chairs of this type. You will receive an offer on request, the duration of the restoration depends on the effort.

product_584.description:
General Information
Bulletproof carpet pad. Felted, not woven
This coaster is made from many small felt balls. The individual balls of pure New Zealand wool are first felted by hand and shaped into their round form and then sewn together - also by hand. As a trivet, the 1.5 centimeter thick felt carpet pad reliably protects the table surface. The fact that the material is more than suitable for this use is due not only to the heat-insulating properties of virgin wool, but also to the fact that virgin wool felt is one of the most flame-retardant natural materials. It is therefore often used as a covering material in aircraft construction, for example. The felt coaster can of course also be used as a base for vases, bowls or dishes to protect the table surface. Or simply as a decorative element.
Fairly combined. Gry & Sif
During her backpacking trip through Nepal, the Dane Gry Staunstrup was immediately captivated by the openness and warmth of the people - and by their craftsmanship. She was able to observe in detail how skillfully and skilfully Nepalese women felted wool into Objekten. The idea of using this skill and combining Nepalese craftsmanship with Danish design was quickly born. And the idea was immediately followed by action.
Since 2000, the company Gry & Sif has been producing a wide range of products from wool felt in Nepal. The designs supplied by Gry Staunstrup are in typical Danish design, as striking as they are discreet and at the same time carefree and cheerful; the production is carried out by Nepalese women using traditional craftsmanship. Now Fair Trade certified, Gry & Sif stands for fair wages, good working conditions and transparency. Only pure new wool from New Zealand sheep is used for the felt products - each of which is unique and handmade.
Note:
Certain manufacturing steps are carried out by hand. Slight dimensional and color deviations may therefore occur.

product_586.description:
General Information
Naturally simple and effective: starch
Nowadays, placemats are mostly made of plastic - due to the common belief that this material alone fulfills its purpose in the (stain) crisis area of table culture. Such opinions may be widespread, but they are not indisputable. And so we found what we were looking for when it came to placemats - at Charvet. The traditional French weaving mill uses an amazingly simple and effective technique that is not without finesse: it treats the surface of the already hard-wearing linen fabric with potato starch, giving it a very high degree of strength. Now, even if people have a perfect command of etiquette in theory, they tend to be a little careless in practice - any resulting stains can be wiped off the starched pure linen placemat with a damp sponge.
From France
For more than 100 years, the Charvet weaving mill has been based in the French town of Armentières, near the border with Flanders. The Nord-Pas-de-Calais region lies at the heart of one of Europe's traditional flax-growing areas. Charvet specialized in the production of linen and cotton fabrics; the product range included robust linen fabrics, which were used to make textiles for bakeries (toiles de boulangerie) and French workwear (e.g. "vareuses" for fishermen), as well as sailcloth fabrics.

product_593.description:
General Information
Gleaming appearance. Jacquard tablecloth with fine luster
On Jacquard looms, the delicate paisley pattern of this linen tablecloth is created. For the linen, yarn from the best European long fiber flax is processed, which is why the jacquard fabric shows a beautiful, delicate shimmering luster - the typical linen luster. The use of undyed linen in the warp and dyed linen yarn in the weft creates a blue background from which the natural colored paisley stands out beautifully. In the natural-colored pattern, the undyed yarn is used in the weft.
Provided all around with a handmade hemstitch, the tablecloth adds festive glamor to your table, but it is just as suitable for (all-)daily use, because linen is dirt-repellent, easy to clean, extremely durable and therefore long-lasting. Only when ironing you should make sure that the linen is still damp - so you protect the fabric and it goes easier from the hand.
Passion for Lithuanian linen. Erika Vaitkute
Erika Vaitkute has been passionate about textiles and fabrics, especially linen, for as long as she can remember. From a young age, she sewed with her mother, who also taught her to appreciate Lithuanian linen. It is important to know that Lithuania has a living and deeply rooted linen tradition dating back thousands of years - it is therefore not unusual for Lithuanians to engage with and continue old textile techniques. On the contrary, in recent years there has been a strong resurgence of interest in them, both throughout the Baltic States and among young artists, designers and craftspeople.
In the meantime, Erika Vaitkute's path (and her sewing machine) has taken her to Germany, but her passion for fine linen textiles and the traditional craft behind them has remained. So she set up a small studio in Hamburg, where she and her team design the patterns and collections. However, the fabrics are still woven and made up in her manufactory in Lithuania. According to all the rules of Lithuanian linen weaving, sophisticated handcrafted pieces are created there, from table linen to hand and kitchen towels to blankets. Only the best linen from long-fiber flax of European origin is used. This not only guarantees the high quality of the linen, but also the careful processing of the ancient crop under fair conditions.

product_611.description:
General Information
Linen is one of the most versatile natural fibers in the textile sector. As table linen, it is often processed in a finer quality. Yet stronger yarn, woven in a looser weave, can create interesting effects. Following our idea, Lino Stilius weaves this table linen especially for Manufactum.
Lively Appearance. Woven Transparency. Washed Linen.
In contrast to freshly starched and ironed table linen, this washed linen has a particularly lively surface. What’s more, Lino Stilius uses somewhat coarser yarns – rather unusual for tablecloths – and has them woven in classic linen weave in a more loosely way. The result is a semi-transparent fabric that appears more voluminous and has a soft touch from the outset, i.e. it no longer shows the initial stiffness typical for linen fabrics.
Lithuanian Linen. A Revived Tradition.
"I love linen and always dreamt of having my own business." Such a statement coming from this young woman might be surprising at first. But when you realise that Kristina Ramanauskaite’s family has been working with linen for thirty years and that she is from Lithuania — a country that has a vibrant, millennia-old, deeply rooted linen tradition — it no longer seems like such an unusual path for her to take. In fact, in recent years the Baltic States have witnessed a growing trend of young artists, designers and artisans reviving old handicraft traditions – a trend that includes Kristina Ramanauskaite.
Lino Stilius — which means “linen style” — is the name of the family business founded in 2011. The Ramanauskaites want to combine the traditions of Lithuanian linen with modern technology and contemporary design. Together with her mother Virginija, Kristina creates simple yet modern linen fabrics that are extremely light, soft and flowing. In order to maintain the natural, slightly wavy appearance of the fabric, it is recommended that after the first wash, you pass a steam iron at the highest temperature over the fabric – without the iron actually touching the fabric, but simply hovering a few millimetres above it.

product_615.description:
General Information
Clear-glass minimalism
The purist form of the Wichernkranz is the Advent wreath: it reduces the countdown to Christmas Eve to the four Sundays of Advent. If you want to go one step further, this striking Advent wreath made of Thuringian forest glass offers minimalism par excellence: a glass ring in which four receptacles for candles or tea lights are recessed - that's all it needs. It draws its high value from the green shimmering material, from the obviously expert care with which the glass mass is poured by hand into the iron mold, and from its massive heaviness. Of course, you can additionally decorate the wreath: The inner round will gladly accept twigs and flowers. In our eyes, however, the Advent wreath already spreads an exquisitely festive mood, when the candlelight in the forest glass resists.
A shimmer of green. Thuringian forest glass
The original type of the famous Thuringian Forest glass is blown and cast at Farbglashütte Lauscha in the south of the Thuringian Forest. The glass originally owes its characteristic green shimmer to the high proportion of iron oxides in the sands of the Thuringian Forest. The raw material for this highly prized glass specialty is melted from this sand, potash and lime. Another typical feature of Thuringian Forest glass is the so-called "Gispen", air bubbles trapped in the glass, which characterize the centuries-old production process in front of the furnace.

product_620.product_name: Hoff terracotta candle holder stackable, Shiny emerald green
product_620.alt_text: Hoff terracotta candle holder stackable, Shiny emerald green
product_620.description:
General Information
Object and light art. Always new
Fired from fine Tuscan terracotta - natural in the typical pink or grey shade or glazed by hand in color - the Hoff candle holders prove themselves as a decorative basis for object and light art full of possibilities. Even as a single piece - as we offer them here - the candle holders have the elegant purism of the straight-lined, clear silhouette that is characteristic of the Hoff collection by Bergs Potter. Designer Anne Hoff follows the modern design language of Scandinavian design, which always keeps the functionality of a design in mind. The candle holders are suitable for both table candles and tea lights - and are decorative eye-catchers on their own. However, you can also combine several candle holders in different stacking heights in a variety of ways, whether you want to accentuate a single color or have several shades harmonize with each other. In this way, you can always create new decorative accents in your room and table design. Of course, the stackability of the Hoff terracotta candle holders is not just a design feature: if you ever want to do without the play of light from candles, the candle holders can be stored to save space.
Plant pots for generations. Bergs Potter in Copenhagen
When Victor Berg inherited his ceramics business in Copenhagen in 1942, it was particularly important to him to make the everyday lives of his fellow human beings a little more colorful in gray times. In the words of the Danish poet Hans Christian Andersen: "Life alone is not enough, said the butterfly. You must have sunshine, freedom and a little flower." So Berg always kept a bouquet of vases and pots in his store and also added cut flowers to the range. The people of Copenhagen liked this - over the years, several stores in the Danish capital were added, and eventually also plant pots and planters based on his own designs. When Victor Berg's children joined the family business in the 1980s, they began to have their own ideas - initially inspired by historical models that they found all over Europe - molded in terracotta. To this end, Bergs Potter still works with traditional potteries in Tuscany, more precisely in Lucca, and now also in Portugal; a tradition that is now being continued with great dedication by the third generation of Bergs. The preferred material is the famous southern Tuscan Galestro clay, which is rich in minerals and is considered to be particularly frost-resistant. Once fired, even the unglazed terracotta can show shades of red and pink, gray and white - an appealing natural patina that only this clay possesses. Another advantage for the health of your potted plants: the carbonate and potassium salts contained in the clay ensure good permeability, which can have a particularly positive effect on the development of the root system.

Certain manufacturing steps are carried out by hand. Slight dimensional and color deviations may therefore occur.

product_621.product_name: Pendant candle holder spring steel, Gold plated
product_621.alt_text: Pendant candle holder spring steel, Gold plated
product_621.description:
General Information
Festivity in balance
Gleaming lights in the Christmas tree is in our eyes absolutely one of the traditions that should be upheld - hardly anything underlines the festive nature of the moment as well as the room illuminated by tree candles. While candles were initially attached to the tree with wax or pins, we have been on the safe(er) side since candle holders for the Christmas tree were patented in the 19th century.
An aesthetically and functionally convincing alternative to clamp candle holders are these asymmetrically shaped pendant candle holders. They are simply hung over the branch and hold themselves and their candle in a vertical position by a counterweight alone. Their design has been known since the early years of pewter, lead or solid brass. Popular forms of the weights were nuts, pine cones or, as in this case, balls - simple, yet effectively shiny.
Inseparable. Like Fest und Lich(t).
The manufacturer, a third-generation family business in Vienna, manufactures the pendant candle holders on a specially adapted spring bending machine from 1.8 mm thick spring steel. This material provides the necessary strength to make the spiral socket of the candle holder break- and tear-resistant.
The brass balls - the manufacturer obtains them from the neighboring turning shop - are assembled manually on the press: The wire is crimped and then the ball is pressed onto the crimped part of the wire. According to the manufacturer, human muscle power will hardly succeed in detaching the pressed-on ball from the wire again. We offer the pendant candle holders in two versions: with silver-plated or gold-plated surface, each including matching drip-free candles.
Please use only drip-free candles. Please make sure never to let the candles burn down completely in the candle holder.
Documents

Height 11 cm. Wire Ø 1.8 mm, ball Ø 1.5 cm. Weight per holder 22 g. The flexible holding tongues accept dripless candles of max. 1.25 cm diameter. Supplied in a box with 10 pendant candle holders and 10 dripless candles (each Ø 1.25 cm, length 9 cm).
Pendant candle holder spring steel wire, nickel plated and gold plated in electroplating bath. Ball brass, nickel-plated and gold-plated in electroplating bath.

General Information
Stable and safe. Again and again
Reuse instead of waste: There is no longer any good reason to use up unmanageable quantities of aluminum in the form of pre-assembled tealight holders, because these stainless steel tealight holders offer a reusable alternative. The cups safely hold standard-sized (Ø 38 mm) bare tealights; once the tealight has burnt down completely, the old wick holder can be removed and the tealight holder can be used again for its intended purpose. Thanks to the typical stability of the material and the long service life of the stainless steel bowls, you can use them again and again, for many atmospheric candlelit evenings, cozy moments of tea enjoyment or soothing wellness baths.
Biokema. Effectively innovative
The careful use of natural resources, the protection of biodiversity and the preservation of ecosystems is the declared aim of the Thuringian company LipiTec, which has developed an innovative option for cascade use. In a patented process, waste fats and oils from the food industry are carefully purified and recycled into a biomass that can be used to produce candles, among other things. Sold under the brand name Biokema, these candles are an impressive example of how recycling can increase raw material efficiency.
With the stainless steel tea light holders, Biokema is taking another important step in this direction, because of course their reusability also conserves natural resources, and of course they are also recyclable - if you ever want to part with them one day in the distant future. After all, stainless steel has a respectable solidity that will do its job in the long term.

Material study.
As a solid piece of bronze, the simple candlestick - the smallest in the Harjes range - is heavy in the hand, its restrained shape bringing out the full beauty of the pure material. For candles up to approx. 12-13 mm Ø, tree candles are best suited.
Cast in bronze

product_632.description:
General Information
Carthusian Handicrafts from Slovenia.
Where do bees get wax from? They secrete it themselves! Bees eat honey. The sugar from the honey is converted into wax by the bee’s special wax-producing glands which make small wax flakes that appear on the bee’s abdomen. These wax scales are then mixed with the bee’s saliva during mastication to soften the wax, which the bee then uses to construct the honeycomb. The honeycomb undergoes several beekeeping processes before pure beeswax is produced. This beautiful set of candles comes from the Carthusians at the Pleterje Charterhouse in Slovenia. If being purchased as a gift, their presentation does away with the need for wrapping paper. The candles are handmade from beeswax from the Carthusians hives. product_643.description:
General Information
The straightness of Bauhaus
Norwegian weaving tradition is combined with the straightforwardness of Bauhaus designs in these pillowcases. In addition to their powerful color palette, the lambswool pillowcases also have a pleasantly soft feel thanks to the roughness of the fabric. Røros Tweed makes them to match our Bauhaus-style blankets: from the same soft Norwegian lambswool.
Norwegian through and through. Røros Tweed
The Norwegian textile company Røros Tweed is characterized by a high level of vertical integration. All production processes, from shearing to weaving, are based in Norway, starting with designs that are created in collaboration with renowned designers, including international ones. The fact that Røros Tweed pays such consistent attention to purely Norwegian production is also due to the appreciation of regional traditions - but not only that.
Exemplary
In Røros, Norway's only mountain town, it all began with a social motivation: the industrialist Peder Hiort (1715-1789) had stipulated in his will that his fortune should be used to buy wool so that the needy of Røros could weave textiles from it in paid homework. Røros Tweed is also part of this tradition of social action and continues the basic idea of the Hiort Foundation - technically advanced and with great care at all levels. The products are designed and manufactured in such a way that the materials used can be reused and returned to the material cycle. This conserves resources, saves material costs and avoids waste.
Wool from Røros
Røros Tweed only uses wool from sheep farms in the region. The sheep live and graze freely on the pasture, even though the climate there is extremely harsh. At the same time, however, this provides a great advantage, as pests do not settle in the wool in the first place. There is therefore no need for chemical treatment. Thanks to the natural living conditions for the sheep, Norwegian new wool has another special feature: It is very elastic. If you squeeze the raw wool with your hands and then let go, it quickly regains its original volume. This elasticity ensures that Røros blankets are so voluminous - and stay that way for a long time.

With Greetings from Mother Goose, Bedtime Bear and Bunny, My Honey.
Most children would probably agree that a stuffed animal must feel soft. The Senger’s geese, bears and rabbits are winners all the way when it comes to being cuddly because the plush fabric made of organic cotton is so fluffy and pleasant to the touch. Volker and Sabine Senger get the pure new sheep's wool for the filling from roving shepherds in the Eifel mountains in the west of Germany whom they know personally. The geese, bears and rabbits are not stuffed too tight though, so that their long legs and arms can swing about when being carried around. The small goose is a particular favourite with small children and is bound to be dragged by the throat across the floor like some kind of “trophy”. Both, small and large goose, are particularly cuddly toys, pillow and warming cushion all in one. Inside each goose, there is a removable cotton pillow. The larger animal, popular not only with children, has a cotton pillow filled with spelt chaff from controlled biological cultivation, while the smaller one contains cherry stones. Amongst other things, heated spelt chaff soothes abdominal pain, while cherry stones, can be used to cool as well as to give warmth. Before heating, the spelt chaff or cherry stone pillow should be removed from the soft toy and then, wrapped in a cotton or linen cloth, heated on the heater, a tile stove or in the oven (maximum temperature: warm to the touch).
Animal dolls to have fun with. Naturally with high standards
It all began in 1985 with a family of mice. The variety of Senger animal dolls has grown to include a rabbit, bear, goose, giraffe, zebra, hedgehog and many others, but Volker and Sabine Senger have remained true to their original conviction to this day: they make toys that are well made and durable. The Senger animal dolls are all made by hand. The owners of the plush toy manufactory, based in the Lower Franconian municipality of Obersinn, also attach great importance to using renewable natural materials without chemical additives or harmful substances: for example, the plush fur of the animals, which is woven in Upper Franconia, is made exclusively from certified organic cotton. The Senger manufactory has already received numerous awards for its commitment to protecting resources.

The history of Røros Tweed
Selected wool from Norwegian sheep and collaborations with leading Scandinavian designers and textile artists have made Røros Tweed one of the most renowned manufacturers of 100% Norwegian branded goods. Røros Tweed, from the UNESCO World Heritage City of Røros in Norway, draws its quality and tradition from a unique history: the testamentary bequest of Peder Hiort, the childless director of the mine, in 1789 led to the establishment of a remarkable foundation. His fortune was used to provide training in textile manufacturing to those in need and to procure the necessary materials. This foundation bought the products of the textile workers and distributed the same garments as alms every year. Often the workers who had been paid for their work received the same garments back. This laid the foundation for a tradition of craftsmanship and textile production that later led to Røros Tweed, which today works closely with renowned Scandinavian designers and textile artists to produce high-quality products from 100% Norwegian wool. The inspiration comes from the surrounding mountain nature and the cultural heritage of Røros. Røros Tweed is known for its curtains, upholstery fabrics, throws and tweed, but the focus today is on high-quality wool blankets that combine tradition and modernity.

product_649.description:
General Information
Heidschnucken fur. From the Lüneburg Heath
This fur comes from Heidschnucken from the Lüneburg Heath, where they are important landscape conservationists. Their meat is prized as a delicacy and is processed into hearty sausages. The Heidschnucken fur is neither bleached nor dyed after tanning. It therefore shows its natural coloring, which ranges from silver-grey and grey to grey-brown to brown. The wool fleece also retains its natural length of between 7 and 15 cm. The Heidschnucken work and graze in their natural life cycle, which is why they are only slaughtered at certain times. It can therefore happen that no skins are available. We also have no influence on the color of your Heidschnucken fur - so the delivery will hold a little surprise.
We source our Heidschnucken furs from the fur specialist Heitmann Felle, a traditional company in the Lüneburg Heath, which was founded in 1820 and is still family-run today (now in its sixth generation). The fur of the Heidschnucken has a rather strong structure, but it is somewhat more sensitive to heavy use than a wool sheepskin, for example. The permanent use as a seat base will therefore become apparent over time. Otherwise, the fur is quite easy to care for: occasional shaking out in the fresh air and careful brushing are sufficient. However, please note that Heidschnucken fur must not be washed or exposed to moisture due to the tanning process. The alum salts used in the tanning process are water-soluble, which is why the leather would become hard when it dries.
Landscape conservationists. No heath without sheep
Heidschnucken characterize the image of the Lüneburg Heath like Erikakraut and Geest. There, they take on the role of landscape caretakers, as their browsing maintains the savannah-like structure and thus the habitat of many plant and animal species, while also fertilizing the soil. Although Heidschnucken are frugal animals, they love variety and like to "snack" on wild herbs and grass as well as heather, which earned them the name "Schnucke", which is derived from "schnökern" - to snack.
The robust Heidschnucken belong to the so-called Nordic short-tailed sheep, and the Lüneburg Heath is primarily home to the gray horned Heidschnucke, which is said to be descended from the mouflon of Sardinia and Corsica. Their fleece (coat) is silver to dark gray, head and chest are black. The horns of the females (the mothers) are twisted backwards in a sickle shape, while the rams' horns are twisted forwards in a snail shape. Heidschnucken lambs are always born with black curls; their wool only changes color to lighter shades between silver-grey and brown in the course of their first year of life. As a mixed-wool land sheep breed, the Heidschnucke has a wool fleece consisting of soft undercoat and coarse awn coat, which protects the undercoat from the weather.

The history of Røros Tweed
Selected wool from Norwegian sheep and collaborations with leading Scandinavian designers and textile artists have made Røros Tweed one of the most renowned manufacturers of 100% Norwegian branded goods. Røros Tweed, from the UNESCO World Heritage City of Røros in Norway, draws its quality and tradition from a unique history: the testamentary bequest of Peder Hiort, the childless director of the mine, in 1789 led to the establishment of a remarkable foundation. His fortune was used to provide training in textile manufacturing to those in need and to procure the necessary materials. This foundation bought the products of the textile workers and distributed the same garments as alms every year. Often the workers who had been paid for their work received the same garments back. This laid the foundation for a tradition of craftsmanship and textile production that later led to Røros Tweed, which today works closely with renowned Scandinavian designers and textile artists to produce high-quality products from 100% Norwegian wool. The inspiration comes from the surrounding mountain nature and the cultural heritage of Røros. Røros Tweed is known for its curtains, upholstery fabrics, throws and tweed, but the focus today is on high-quality wool blankets that combine tradition and modernity.

product_652.description:
General Information
Modern garb for Norwegian tradition
The Norwegian designers Torbjørn Anderssen and Espen Voll are an established name in Scandinavia, their designs internationally renowned. They have a long-standing partnership with Røros Tweed - the duo designed the first blanket designs for Røros Tweed when they founded their label Norway Says. In the meantime, Anderssen & Voll have received several awards for their work, including for some of their Røros designs. Tradition and modern trends inspire them equally and flow into their timeless designs.
The Fri design is heavily inspired by the Norwegian tradition of small, rectangular tablecloths called "løpere." Variations of these textiles can be found in almost every Norwegian mountain hut. Typical is the repeating color rhythm, which is somewhat broken up in this interpretation for Røros Tweed: The colors shift seemingly at random on a soft zigzag pattern. The Fri pillowcases are woven from soft Norwegian lambswool, and all edges are worked with a small standing seam. The matching lambswool blankets with the same pattern can also be found in our range.
Norwegian through and through. Røros Tweed
The Norwegian textile company Røros Tweed is characterized by a high level of vertical integration. All production processes, from shearing to weaving, are based in Norway, starting with designs that are created in collaboration with renowned designers, including international ones. The fact that Røros Tweed pays such consistent attention to purely Norwegian production is also due to the appreciation of regional traditions - but not only that.
Exemplary
In Røros, Norway's only mountain town, it all began with a social motivation: the industrialist Peder Hiort (1715-1789) had stipulated in his will that his fortune should be used to buy wool so that the needy of Røros could weave textiles from it in paid homework. Røros Tweed is also part of this tradition of social action and continues the basic idea of the Hiort Foundation - technically advanced and with great care at all levels. The products are designed and manufactured in such a way that the materials used can be reused and returned to the material cycle. This conserves resources, saves material costs and avoids waste.
Wool from Røros
Røros Tweed only uses wool from sheep farms in the region. The sheep live and graze freely on the pasture, even though the climate there is extremely harsh. At the same time, however, this provides a great advantage, as pests do not settle in the wool in the first place. There is therefore no need for chemical treatment. Thanks to the natural living conditions for the sheep, Norwegian new wool has another special feature: It is very elastic. If you squeeze the raw wool with your hands and then let go, it quickly regains its original volume. This elasticity ensures that Røros blankets are so voluminous - and stay that way for a long time.

Haunold®. Walkfelt with brains
Behind the Haunold® brand stands the Zacher family from San Candido, which has been active as craftsmen since 1560 and thus runs the oldest craft business in South Tyrol. At present, it is the five siblings Johann, Hedwig, Alois, Friedrich and Christina who, together with three employees, produce first-class fulling felt products. Today's business goes back to a millinery that came into the family around 1850. The wool felts and felt slippers are still produced there according to the old millinery tradition - which is why the Zachers still feel they belong to the millinery trade. The rolling of the felt slippers is still done on the old hammer mill, which the great-grandfather had made in 1901 and which has been in continuous use ever since. Incidentally, the brand name Haunold® comes from the local mountain of the municipality of San Candido, a Dolomite peak located in the immediate vicinity of the famous Three Peaks.

Brass Lights from Berlin.

Hand-Painted Decors.
When switched off, the shades are bright white; when switched on, they shimmer silkily and warm in colour. At BTC’s, an experienced employee decorates the lampshades by hand with the different line patterns. Bowles hired her when her previous employer, a big player in the industry, gave up hand-painting. Since then, Bowles has been making the hand-painted lamps simply because he wants to and his employee can.
British, in Detail. Lamps from BTC.
Lamps made by BTC (= British Timeless Classics), in the vicinity of Oxford, have attained the status of timeless classics. The creative spirit and driving force behind the firm is Peter Bowles, who pursues his very clear idea and just as clearly realises his agenda. The process starts with the manufacture: Bowles wants to produce lamps that are British down to the level of detail. For example, the bone china-lamp shades come from a pottery in Stoke-on-Trent, known as the "the Potteries" because of the almost 500 potteries that used to be located there. Almost all are gone today and the firm, which also belongs to Bowles, would not exist except for BTC. He took it over when it was on the brink of bankruptcy and has restructured it while keeping all the employees. The hand-blown glass domes come from a glass blowing shop in Worcestershire which Bowles also bought. In addition to domes for lamps, the shop produces coloured glass windows for historical buildings and churches. A handful of glass blowers with their two small smelting furnaces practice the methods of glass blowing and uphold the once famous English tradition of this trade. The British manufacture of the lamps extends to the cables, too. Bowles was dissatisfied with the plastic wrapped cables on his first lamp, so he used a locally produced cloth wrapped cable from a clothes iron for his exhibition piece. The reaction was so positive that he has used cloth cable since. They are locally produced near the firm in home-based work.

General Information
Small effort, big effect. The Linestra
From an ugly duckling - the S14d socket from Osram with the euphonious name "670 socket GR 250V UNV1" - Mawa has made this beautiful swan: by wrapping the drab gray raw body with a neat little steel coat. In use, the main actor of this luminaire is indeed clearly the 50 cm long, line lamp called illuminant in the dimensions of a fluorescent tube. But thanks to Mawa, the luminaire itself is also well worth a closer look. In its parade role as a mirror luminaire (mounted to the right and left of the mirror), it evenly illuminates those reflected in the mirror when equipped with a matt rod lamp; with a clear rod lamp, it succeeds even more spectacularly. We offer the lamp in three versions, with the surface of the copper-plated and brass-plated variant clear overpainted.
Lighting for Living Areas and Museum Exhibitions. Mawa Design.
Mawa Design was founded in 1977 by Martin Wallroth in Berlin-Kreuzberg. Wallroth initially developed and produced objects for the living area and often played a pioneering role for formative ideas in product design. In the 1980s, he began fruitful collaborations with external designers excelling at bringing product ideas quickly to commercial viability thanks to the company’s flexible structure. While diligently producing the various serial models, Mawa customized a selection of products to different specifications: Luminaires for the master houses at the Bauhaus Dessau, the home of Corbusier, the University of the Arts and the Maxim Gorki Theatre in Berlin, the Treptow Crematorium and the Luther House in Wittenberg were among them. And last but not least, museums worldwide present Mawa luminaires, renowned for high-quality materials and unsurpassed technical implementation, as parts of their collections.
Combining Manufacture Skills and High-Technology Knowledge.
Mawa luminaires have always been at the cutting edge of light design while excelling at the technical execution and directing the light with regard to the fancied visual impact. Groundbreaking innovations in the lighting sector, such as the LED filament light bulbs, immediately found their way into the Mawa product cosmos. A decisive factor in the entrepreneurial success of Mawa Design was (and still is) the extraordinary combination of design studio and manufactory. Since 1997, the company has been based in the Palmhof, a renovated and listed historical monument in Langerwisch near Potsdam. Eventually, the manufactory offers enough space for all employees and the creation and production of the numerous in-house designs such as the wall and mirror lamp “Linestra”, the wall and ceiling lamps “Etna” and “Eintopf”, plus lighting classics of other renowned designers such as the pendant lamp “Havanna” designed by Wilhelm Braun-Feldweg or the floor lamp “Schliephacke” named after its creator.

product_700.description:
General Information
From England: Bone China Lamps.
‘Bone China’ is one of the noblest porcelains. It’s a bright white, extremely thin yet practically unbreakable. Its most surprising property is perhaps the way it lets through the light – shimmering like satin and with a warm glow. The secret Chinese recipe for making bone china was cracked by a stone factory in England in the middle of the 18th century – the addition of bone ash in the firing process. This, and other ingredients like quartz-sand, render the whole production process far from easy. Mass-production is impossible, and the number of firms that have the necessary manufacturing skills is limited. We’ve found such a firm in England that possesses real ‘craftsman skills!
British, in Detail. Lamps from BTC.
Lamps made by BTC (= British Timeless Classics), in the vicinity of Oxford, have attained the status of timeless classics. The creative spirit and driving force behind the firm is Peter Bowles, who pursues his very clear idea and just as clearly realises his agenda. The process starts with the manufacture: Bowles wants to produce lamps that are British down to the level of detail. For example, the bone china-lamp shades come from a pottery in Stoke-on-Trent, known as the "the Potteries" because of the almost 500 potteries that used to be located there. Almost all are gone today and the firm, which also belongs to Bowles, would not exist except for BTC. He took it over when it was on the brink of bankruptcy and has restructured it while keeping all the employees. The hand-blown glass domes come from a glass blowing shop in Worcestershire which Bowles also bought. In addition to domes for lamps, the shop produces coloured glass windows for historical buildings and churches. A handful of glass blowers with their two small smelting furnaces practice the methods of glass blowing and uphold the once famous English tradition of this trade. The British manufacture of the lamps extends to the cables, too. Bowles was dissatisfied with the plastic wrapped cables on his first lamp, so he used a locally produced cloth wrapped cable from a clothes iron for his exhibition piece. The reaction was so positive that he has used cloth cable since. They are locally produced near the firm in home-based work.
Please note:
The angle of the lamp can be changed: but the operation of the angling screw is so simple that both shade and light fixture can fall out if you go to work too enthusiastically. So: be careful and above all gentle when adjusting the angle!

product_701.description:
General Information
High-quality light tube with professional lighting technology for wall mounting and free positioning in the room. The housing, co-extruded from polycarbonate and sealed with stainless steel caps, houses a linear LED strip whose light is glare-free and directed downwards using angled aluminum blades. A reflective aluminum reflector inserted at the rear additionally amplifies the light. The result is a well-dosed, flat light that is pleasing to the eye and ideal for use as additional lighting or a reading lamp next to the sofa, bed or in an alcove. The transparent tube reveals the technical parts of the luminaire - light unit, aluminium louvre and reflector - and thus ensures the technical and industrial character of the luminaire. The mounting solution for the iconic luminaire is as simple as it is beautiful: it is inserted into two stainless steel clips that can be mounted on the wall and fixed in place using the integrated buckles. ELGAR has a 200 cm long cable with a Euro plug, so it can be positioned anywhere in the room. The light is switched on and dimmed continuously using the round push-button on the top. Practical: the built-in LED strip can be replaced by the manufacturer. Made in France, the luminaire contains LEDs. Rated power: 5 W (silver-colored version) or 7 W (petrol-colored version), color temperature: 2,700 K, luminous flux: 430 lm, color rendering: CRI >80, dimmable, protection rating: IP65. Cable: L 200 cm, Euro plug (type C).
Lights from Sammode Studio
The French luminaire manufacturer SAMMODE originally specialized in lighting solutions that are used wherever it is too hot, too cold, too dusty, too wet or even explosive for conventional luminaires - in industrial plants, laboratories, cold rooms and all outdoor areas, but also in museums and libraries. Because the special aesthetics of the tubular luminaires, which are made of glass or polycarbonate and encapsulated in stainless steel depending on their intended use, aroused the interest of architects, SAMMODE has also been making a name for itself for several years with luminaires for the home. The tubular luminaires have been domesticated, so to speak, and rededicated or redesigned as wall and ceiling luminaires. The French manufacturer's home lighting range now includes a whole spectrum of different lighting solutions. The luminaires are manufactured in Châtillon-sur-Saône in the Vosges, where SAMMODE was founded in 1927 as the "Société d'Application des Méthodes Modernes d'Éclairage électrique".

While diligently producing the various serial models, Mawa customized a selection of products to different specifications: Luminaires for the master houses at the Bauhaus Dessau, the home of Corbusier, the University of the Arts and the Maxim Gorki Theatre in Berlin, the Treptow Crematorium and the Luther House in Wittenberg were among them. A decisive factor in the entrepreneurial success of Mawa Design was (and still is) the extraordinary combination of design studio and manufactory. Eventually, the manufactory offers enough space for all employees and the creation and production of the numerous in-house designs such as the wall and mirror lamp “Linestra”, the wall and ceiling lamps “Etna” and “Eintopf”, plus lighting classics of other renowned designers such as the pendant lamp “Havanna” designed by Wilhelm Braun-Feldweg or the floor lamp “Schliephacke” named after its creator.

Sturdy universal solution
Seat and step stool as well as side table and bedside table in one: This small universal piece of furniture made of solid wood is versatile and impresses above all with its stable construction: To ensure that the furniture can also withstand greater loads (for example in its function as a step), it is: 1. Radically simple, completely functional: furniture from Auerberg

These are handcrafted products that are designed away from industrial standards, far removed from fashion and uninfluenced by marketing constraints and produced in small batches. Behind every single piece of furniture is the authentic personality of the respective designer - and because there is no restrictive program dictate, the product designers are only committed to their own standards. Accordingly, all Auerberg furniture is unmistakable, sometimes purist to the point of stubbornness, extremely solid in terms of craftsmanship and thus virtually made to last.
The furniture is manufactured regionally in Upper Bavaria and the wood - mostly oak, ash and beech - comes from certified forestry operations. The mastermind behind Auerberg is Christoph Böninger, once a professional globetrotter, now a settled design publisher. Well-connected in design circles, Böninger works in Munich and on his farm in Auerberg - hence the name of the project - near Bad Aibling. And even though Böninger has gathered a number of designers and architects around him for his "product lab" - with established greats standing alongside up-and-coming talent - he still lends a hand himself. Sometimes he oils wooden furniture and gets it ready for shipping. Incidentally, Auerberg's greatest successes to date include the AEKI step stool by Gerhardt Kellermann and the "Silent Ladder" by Christoph Böninger himself, a versatile hybrid of stepladder and silent servant.

General Information
Less space. More use
From wall projection to stand-alone piece of furniture: the functional value of the console table is clear from its origins. Its shallow depth makes it ideal for smaller rooms or the alcove of a larger room, where it blends in modestly but still attracts attention and use - especially when it has a high-quality finish like this one. And since, unlike a console, it is not permanently installed, you can place the console table wherever you like, whether as a storage unit in the hallway or bedroom, as a side table in the dining room or office or as a small home office station in the living room.
Thanks to its elegant, minimalist design - which does not deny its proximity to mid-century modern with its slender, slightly flared table legs - this table blends in with many furnishing styles, regardless of whether you prefer a minimalist or more playful interior design. The solid oak wood proves the lasting value of the classic handcrafted construction, in which the table top is made from continuous slats. The drawer creates additional storage space and is of course just as carefully crafted: Made of sturdy poplar plywood and birch plywood, it is guided on precisely fitted beechwood rails without fogging. And with the natural grain of its solid oak panel, it also blends smoothly into the look of the console table.
The quality of the craftsmanship speaks for itself, right down to the steel fittings on the frames and legs. The console table is delivered disassembled - but you only have to screw the table legs to the table frames yourself. Assembly is done quickly and, most importantly, is carried out using machine screws and threaded sleeves. In contrast to conventional grub screws, this connection is very stable and can be loosened and re-screwed as often as you like, without knocking out and losing accuracy of fit and cohesion.

product_717.description:
General Information
Practical version of the original: In 1965, in Egon Eiermann's environment, a dismountable version of the original Eiermann table frame was created in the locksmith's shop at Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences - an interpretation that was not Egon Eiermann's own idea, but was initiated by one of his assistants. Unlike the original, the cross does not sit in the sloping space, but at right angles between the side sections. The cross brace tubes are bolted together back to back and to the side sections via the tube segments welded to their ends. A practical side effect: by raising the cross struts, more storage and leg space is created under the table top. The height and angle of the table top can be individually adjusted using the extension rods supplied: The rods are 33.5 cm long, have 5 adjustment options and allow working heights from 72 cm to 86 cm. If two of the rods are set higher than the other two, the table top can also be set at an angle. We offer the frame with an eccentrically positioned cross, including long extension rods and rubber stoppers.
Egon Eiermann - architect and designer
Egon Fritz Wilhelm Eiermann, born in Neuendorf near Berlin in 1904, is considered one of the most important German architects of post-war modernism. His residential buildings from the 1930s, the handkerchief weaving mill in Blumberg in 1951, St. Matthew's Church in Pforzheim in 1953, the German Pavilion at the World Exhibition in Brussels in 1958, the new Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church in Berlin in 1961, the German Embassy in Washington in 1964, the high-rise parliament building in Bonn in 1969 and the administration buildings for IBM and Olivetti in Stuttgart and Frankfurt in 1970 are among his most important buildings.Eiermann was a full professor at the Faculty of Architecture at the Technical University in Karlsruhe, where he ran his own architectural practice and also designed numerous pieces of furniture during this time. These included his archetypal tubular steel table frame in 1953, with whose reduced construction Eiermann - coming from the field of architecture - found the optimum combination of material use and stability. Designed as a work table that could not be dismantled, the original served as the basis for various further developments. In 1965, for example, a demountable version with a decentrally mounted and vertically aligned cross was created, followed later by a version that can also be used as a dining table and a small version for children by manufacturer Richard Lampert and in exchange with Eiermann's descendants.

Series Container DS
Synonymous with storage and transport: the container in its archetypal surface of folded steel. We offer this cabinet furniture in the miniaturized form of overseas containers in four different versions. These well-proportioned storage boxes serve many purposes and areas of use. All containers have perforations in the bottoms for passing cables. The classic container as well as the flat and small container have doors hinged to the top of the body, which slide into the top of the body when opened and thus almost completely disappear. The CONTAINER DS PLUS is upright and has a conventional hinged door on the side.
The classic: The CONTAINER DS in the proportion of a sea container is virtually the archetype of the series CONTAINER DS. It serves as a cabinet in the living room for china and utensils for the set table, in the office for storing files in standardized format or for paper and office utensils. The coat rack completes the container to a functional wardrobe. The container of this format is available in limited color selection equipped with a lock. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The flat one: CONTAINER DS FLAT has the footprint of the classic CONTAINER DS and can be connected to it in height and stacked. It can be combined with the above mentioned accessories of the classic CONTAINER DS. This container often serves as a flat element that is built into a stack of the classic container. It is useful with its special volume for the stack of paper, for utensils and as a shelf for many purposes. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The small one: The CONTAINER DS KLEIN as the little brother of the CONTAINER DS does not have the proportions of a sea container, unlike its archetypal big role model - it is narrower, with identical depth and height. With its small size and unusual formatting, it serves as a piece of side furniture next to the bed and sofa and can also be stacked up to form a tower. It can be equipped with all separate feet as well as the casters. Unlike its sister models, it is always equipped with a smooth cover shelf in the respective color. It can be used in portrait format and serves as a locker-like clothes or wardrobe cabinet and can also be used as a large-volume cabinet, individually or stacked on top of each other in the kitchen, office or other places. This drawer, like the stool itself, is made of untreated spruce wood, worked with dovetailed edges and equipped with a simple but effective pull-out stop. Authentic aesthetics. Stained in color
Three wooden planks that are connected to form a U by finger joints and stabilized on the open side by a round crossbar - the Ulm stool is an impressive example of the art of designing an extremely minimalist and yet multifunctional construction: it can be used as a seat, side table, shelf or carrying aid for books and the like. Designed in the mid-1950s by Max Bill, Bauhaus student, architect and at the time Rector of the Ulm School of Design, in collaboration with Hans Gugelot and Paul Hildinger, the Ulm stool is undisputedly one of the icons of furniture design.
And while its areas of application regularly open up new perspectives, the Ulm Stool itself is also being given a new look. While the original was made from untreated spruce planks - also available from us in this original material - we are now expanding our range to include a colored version made from birch and beech wood. To achieve an authentic aesthetic, the wood is stained in color, not varnished, so that the grain of the wood can still shine through. The famous solid construction has remained the same, as has the production in Switzerland.

Great classic for small: The small version of the table frame designed by Egon Eiermann grows with you, as it is adjustable in height. The table top can be screwed to the supporting rods of the table frame with the help of an enclosed accessory.
Egon Eiermann - architect and designer
Egon Fritz Wilhelm Eiermann, born in Neuendorf near Berlin in 1904, is considered one of the most important German architects of post-war modernism. His residential buildings from the 1930s, the handkerchief weaving mill in Blumberg in 1951, St. Matthew's Church in Pforzheim in 1953, the German Pavilion at the World Exhibition in Brussels in 1958, the new Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church in Berlin in 1961, the German Embassy in Washington in 1964, the high-rise parliament building in Bonn in 1969 and the administration buildings for IBM and Olivetti in Stuttgart and Frankfurt in 1970 are among his most important buildings.Eiermann was a full professor at the Faculty of Architecture at the Technical University in Karlsruhe, where he ran his own architectural practice and also designed numerous pieces of furniture during this time. These included his archetypal tubular steel table frame in 1953, with whose reduced construction Eiermann - coming from the field of architecture - found the optimum combination of material use and stability. Designed as a work table that could not be dismantled, the original served as the basis for various further developments. In 1965, for example, a demountable version with a decentrally mounted and vertically aligned cross was created, followed later by a version that can also be used as a dining table and a small version for children by manufacturer Richard Lampert and in exchange with Eiermann's descendants.

product_739.description:
General Information
Beautiful, simple, Scandinavian
Scandinavian design is functional and of simple elegance, it is aesthetically pleasing and practical. Made from natural materials, usually in light colors, it fits into almost any style of living and contributes to a friendly atmosphere. No wonder we have a soft spot for furniture from Scandinavia. We were also impressed by this simple model from Danish manufacturer Form & Refine. The highlight here: The side table has two levels, the top of which has a recess so that you can place magazines, Magazine and books. A more than clever design, as it not only saves space, but also nerves, because the items can be pulled out individually without dragging others along (as often happens with stacks). The cleat construction ensures load-bearing capacity: Two "table tops" and two side panels made of glued oak slats are set into the four solid oak posts. The surfaces are veneered for evenness. There is no need to emphasize the fact that everything has been carefully crafted; the attention to detail is also evident in the side panels of the shelves, for example. They ensure harmonious proportions and, together with the side panels, form a frame that prevents the items placed on or off the shelves from falling overboard (at least it reduces the risk of falling).
Form & Refine. Danish design
Form & Refine is a Danish design label founded in 2018 by Helle Herman Mortensen, Jonas Herman Pedersen and Lasse Lund Lauridsen. It exemplarily follows the Scandinavian design tradition and continues it at the same time. A central point is the harmonious combination of aesthetics, function and material. The designs are clear and restrained, function leads to form and the pure materials, which are allowed to retain their original visual details and forms, are processed with perfect craftsmanship. This is always done in the countries of origin of the materials, which shortens transport distances and at the same time supports the local craft culture.

product_750.description:
General Information
The PLICO serving trolley designed by Richard Sapper in the 1970s is one of his lesser-known projects, although it is one of his strongest designs. His more popular designs include the TIZIO work lamp and the ZOOM BIKE, which folds to a minimal size. Sapper was a master of construction and a great lover of so-called collapsibles. These space-saving products can be folded or modified thanks to their design, making them more versatile in their application. Sapper himself declared it an essential goal of his design work to solve and eliminate problems or defects that can be identified in existing objects. PLICO is handy and extremely compact when folded. Simply grab the top shelf and pull it upwards - and the furniture folds up. When folded, PLICO takes up minimal space and can be placed behind the kitchen door or between two pieces of kitchen furniture, for example, and remains stable thanks to the brakes on the rear wheels. It can be used in a variety of ways, as a serving trolley, as a side table by the bed or sofa or as a small, extremely flexible work table where you want to sit with your laptop and also need shelves for this and that work utensil. The top surface can be folded down in one simple movement, completely changing the structure of the trolley. The shelf now protrudes slightly above the trolley and serves as a usable surface. The structure of the serving trolley is made of black lacquered steel. The shelves are made of matt black lacquered thermoplastic resin, a very high-quality and durable plastic. Four rubber-coated castors, two of which can be steered and two of which have locking brakes, also glide over textile floors. Max. load weight: lower shelf: 7 kg, upper shelf: 4 kg or 12 kg.

product_751.description:
General Information
Creative embrace. For many purposes
The basic structure of this multipurpose furniture made of molded plywood is composed of two parts of different sizes. When put together, the construct can be used as a side or coffee table, small shelf, seating or television furniture; when taken apart, the smaller of the two elements can be used as a bed or laptop tray, for example. Both together function as a table and bench for children. Thanks to cut-out inserts, the individual parts are easily transportable and can thus be spontaneously repurposed. The furniture was designed by the British designer John Green in York - given that Isokon (now Isokon plus), one of the most renowned molded plywood furniture pioneers, is based on the island, the origin of this simple and at the same time beautiful design seems hardly surprising.Green heeds all the rules that must be followed when building affordable plywood furniture: -few individual parts, -as little complex forming as possible - that is, none at all or two-dimensional, -as few joints as possible, and -few complex joining techniques. The application of these premises manifests itself in Green's multipurpose furniture, which bears the evocative name "embrace", as follows: It consists of two plywood parts, each deformed in two dimensions, with two incisions on the sides that allow the two elements to be plugged together.

product_769.description:
General Information
For Glare-Free Illumination.
These brass lights from Berlin illuminat with a maximum of 200 watts of corridor, living room and bedroom. Due to the upwardly open shape, the most of the stray light is reflected from the ceiling. As a result, a good and glare-free illumination of the room is achieved. The interior design of the luminaire also allows the use of energy-saving lamps.
Brass Lights from Berlin.
The Berlin lighting manufacturers had their heyday at the beginning of the 20th century, the imprint of the Art Nouveau style is unmistakable. You will notice how good these lights are at the very moment when you set them up respectively hang them up: The metal parts are made of solid brass or, in the case of long pipes, made of brass plated steel. The lampshades are made of hand-blown glass; they gain their shape in wooden forms. The electrical leads are solid textile cables. The ceiling roses are made of porcelain or brass. The patina dyed brass is not lacquered, so the patina can be partially or entirely removed by careful brushing with fine steel wool to emphasize contours or to heighten the shine. A trace of olive oil, applied with a lint-free cloth, is all the care the brass needs. Unlike the most uninhibitedly historicised replicas, the Berlin brass lights are of timeless clarity.

General Information
Glassworks Limburg.
The Limburg glass foundry is one of the most renowned lamp glass manufacturers in Europe. product_790.alt_text: Hinged drawer container, sheet steel, 5 compartments, anthracite
product_790.description:
General Information
Home Smart Home. Container with a future
Its design is reminiscent of the utopias of the 1960s, its construction has reached maturity, its choice of materials is more sophisticated than ever before and its functionality is as flexible as visionaries could wish for.
Called a "pivot cabinet" in English, this name - "pivot" means "pivot joint" or "swivel axis" - refers to the essential design element of the container: the individual drawers are swung open on an axis, not pulled open or folded down as is usually the case. This design idea was made famous by Joe Colombo's "Boby" roll container developed in 1970. The Italian architect was also one of the leading futuristic industrial designers of the 1960s, a time of optimism and visions of the future, which - following Herbert Marcuse's train of thought, for example - sought to pave the way out of the realm of necessity and into the realm of freedom. Designs such as Verner Panton's cantilever "Panton Chair", Olivier Mourgue's "Djinn" armchair, which adorned the interior of "2001 - A Space Odyssey", and Colombo's "Tube Chair" became icons. Colombo's "dynamic pieces of furniture" always aimed to be multifunctional.
Our swivel drawer container builds on the ideal of those designs, but doesn't just quote the utopias of past decades, but smartly brings the future into your home today. While Colombo and his colleagues were still enthusiastic about the newly developed plastics of the 1960s, we know better today and prefer sheet steel, which offers far greater stability and durability. The sheet steel thus reinforces the versatility of the container. In the kitchen, bathroom, living room or entrance area - sturdy and stable, the hinged drawer container performs its intended functions of storage, presentation and easy access in any environment and, like any successful design object, catches the eye perfectly without imposing itself on the other furniture.
With an undivided surface area of around A4, the revolving drawers can hold larger and smaller good things. The construction is well thought out and solid: The front round steel, which connects the top cover and base of the container, forms the swivel axis so that the drawers are flush with the rear steel tubes when closed; with the help of a small magnet on the rear wall, they dock into place with a gentle snap. And even if they don't beep or flash to let you know that the fridge needs to be refilled, the drawers reveal all the necessary and possible contents by swiveling open 270 degrees and providing a complete overview. At the bottom, the height-adjustable feet ensure that you can counteract any unevenness in the surface. And if you want to make your designer furniture even more mobile, we offer a separate set of castor feet for the swivel drawer container, which you can screw into place of the feet in no time at all.
Attention:
Please observe the maximum permissible load capacity of the revolving drawers. Distribute the weight evenly. Heavier objects should be placed in the lower, lighter ones in the upper revolving drawers. Do not open more than one revolving drawer at a time to avoid tipping over. Do not leave small children unattended with this piece of furniture.
