product_795.description:
General Information
Multiple benefits
Spacious catch basin for discarded desk papers, used towels or even the knitting next to the couch: this basket impresses with its versatile use, its natural materiality and, last but not least, its extremely attractive appearance. Even purists who think in terms of material economy will get their money's worth here, because despite its visual and functional opulence, the design of this paper and laundry basket impresses with its well thought-out minimalism. A three-layer thick veneer sheet is bent to form an almost cylindrical body, interlocked to maintain its shape and glued to the circular base plate; the upper edge is reinforced by an inner ring made of three-layer wood. Covered with a fine layer of clear varnish so that the individual grain stands out even more beautifully, the result is a stable lightweight that can be carried around effortlessly using the two side handles - if you don't want to take your eyes off this simple beauty (or simply want to transport the towels to the washing machine).
Tradition x modernity. Mint Furniture
Anyone who still thinks that traditional craftsmanship results in furniture à la Gelsenkirchen Baroque should turn their gaze to Riga. There, the company Mint Furniture, founded in 2009, stands for furniture design in which the tried and tested is taken up and further developed in form and function. This is the essence of innovation anyway, especially when it wants to stand out from the mass of supposed modernity in a visionary way. The team at Mint Furniture, which combines knowledge of fine art, interior design, industrial design and craftsmanship, has also achieved something astonishing: an individual design signature that is revealed in the fine details. With his spindle stool made of solid oak, co-founder Janis Rauza laid the foundation for the creative combination of formal tradition and functional modernity. Continuously expanded, the entire furniture collection from Mint Furniture follows this vision: expertly crafted by cabinetmakers, supported by a profound knowledge of the possibilities of the material and supported by the use of modern technologies, the designs point far into the future as pieces for generations.

product_798.description:
General Information
Servant ladder
The somewhat cryptic name of this small piece of furniture - silent ladder - is decoded with the information that it is a hybrid (conceived from the ladder) of stepladder and silent servant, which is intended to fulfill both functions. In its role as a ladder, it has two steps together with a safety bar - in ladder construction, this is the name given to the combination of stiles extended in the direction of stepping and a cross connection. As a mute servant, the furniture from Auerberg in Bavaria offers space for a shirt (thrown over the top; the ash wood stiles have a semi-circular cross-section especially for this purpose) and trousers (these can be hung over the rung that cannot be stepped on). The two lower steps and a small leather-lined compartment for trouser pockets on top serve as storage areas. Further re-purposing is not excluded.
Radically simple, completely functional: furniture from Auerberg
Radical reduction in form and material and a complete focus on function - that is the guiding principle behind the furniture from Auerberg. These are handcrafted products that are designed away from industrial standards, far removed from fashion and uninfluenced by marketing constraints and produced in small batches. Behind every single piece of furniture is the authentic personality of the respective designer - and because there is no restrictive program dictate, the product designers are only committed to their own standards. Accordingly, all Auerberg furniture is unmistakable, sometimes purist to the point of stubbornness, extremely solid in terms of craftsmanship and thus virtually made to last.
The furniture is manufactured regionally in Upper Bavaria and the wood - mostly oak, ash and beech - comes from certified forestry operations. The mastermind behind Auerberg is Christoph Böninger, once a professional globetrotter, now a settled design publisher. Well-connected in design circles, Böninger works in Munich and on his farm in Auerberg - hence the name of the project - near Bad Aibling. And even though Böninger has gathered a number of designers and architects around him for his "product lab" - with established greats standing alongside up-and-coming talent - he still lends a hand himself. Sometimes he oils wooden furniture and gets it ready for shipping. Incidentally, Auerberg's greatest successes to date include the AEKI step stool by Gerhardt Kellermann and the "Silent Ladder" by Christoph Böninger himself, a versatile hybrid of stepladder and silent servant.

product_801.description:
General Information
carrier, storage box, stool and side table
This small piece of furniture made of Bavarian oak and ash wood is intended for various functions, which are almost fully described with sitting and drinking. Generically, it is a support for eight bottles of wine or water, which can optionally serve to transport or store the same. Turned upside down or sideways, it becomes a stool (on which you can rest, for example, from carrying bottles over long distances) or a side table, depending on the position, with the option of storing a supply of wine.
Its remarkable aesthetic appeal results from the contrasts created by its construction and choice of materials: between the vivid light ash wood and the darker oak of the bottle frame as well as the round bar acting as a handle, between the grain of the ash wood and its end wood surfaces, which are visible because of the side parts that are positively joined to the base. Designed in 2015 by Christoph Böninger, the piece is manufactured by Auerberg in Bavaria and has since found its way into the Neue Sammlung in Munich.
Radically simple, completely functional: furniture from Auerberg
Radical reduction in form and material and a complete focus on function - that is the guiding principle behind the furniture from Auerberg. These are handcrafted products that are designed away from industrial standards, far removed from fashion and uninfluenced by marketing constraints and produced in small batches. Behind every single piece of furniture is the authentic personality of the respective designer - and because there is no restrictive program dictate, the product designers are only committed to their own standards. Accordingly, all Auerberg furniture is unmistakable, sometimes purist to the point of stubbornness, extremely solid in terms of craftsmanship and thus virtually made to last.
The furniture is manufactured regionally in Upper Bavaria and the wood - mostly oak, ash and beech - comes from certified forestry operations. The mastermind behind Auerberg is Christoph Böninger, once a professional globetrotter, now a settled design publisher. Well-connected in design circles, Böninger works in Munich and on his farm in Auerberg - hence the name of the project - near Bad Aibling. And even though Böninger has gathered a number of designers and architects around him for his "product lab" - with established greats standing alongside up-and-coming talent - he still lends a hand himself. Sometimes he oils wooden furniture and gets it ready for shipping. Incidentally, Auerberg's greatest successes to date include the AEKI step stool by Gerhardt Kellermann and the "Silent Ladder" by Christoph Böninger himself, a versatile hybrid of stepladder and silent servant.

The Ulm Stool - designed in 1955 by Max Bill, the first director of the Ulm University of Design, in collaboration with Hans Gugelot and Paul Hildinger for the students* of this very university - is a furniture as simple as it is multifunctional. General Information
Imaginative fun
If your children cast a covetous eye on this decorative strip, don't be surprised. After all, the strip was originally developed as a toy: to support our offspring in their free play in accordance with the principles of Montessori education, to allow them to develop their individual potential and to train their motor and cognitive skills. We are now convinced that the strip also has great decorative qualities and that you can give free rein to your own imagination by placing - and repositioning - the treetops as you wish.
Each of the five treetops has a different shape - hemisphere, cone, ellipse, column or umbrella - so that you can achieve a different effect with each new combination. In addition to the visual experience, the decorative strip offers you an equally fine tactile pleasure when you rearrange it: The base is made of fine-pored maple wood, the tree trunks and crowns are made of beech wood and all surfaces have been sanded and oiled by hand to a velvety smooth finish. And if you're not adding other decorative ideas to your delicate yet solid tree arrangement - such as twigs, leaves and flowers, colorful cards, origami or felt objects - you can of course let the younger members of your family try out a new combination.
The story of the forest. Told by a toy
The Polish family business Wooden Story stands for toys made from certified wood. As befits a family from the forests of the Makov Beskids, Wooden Story also begins with a forest spirit - at least its name. Slavic mythology tells of the forest spirit Borowy, who protects forests and game. Coincidence or not, the founding family of Wooden Story is also called Borowy, and under the expert hands of grandfather Borowy, the company's first wooden toy was created in 1969.
Now in its fourth generation, the family business, which has since established itself with its natural wood furniture, is once again manufacturing wooden toys. The joy of creating for children and the respectful attitude towards nature are reflected in these toys. Wooden Story produces exclusively from certified wood of European origin, to which natural pigments lend color. And instead of sealing artificial varnishes, the surface is given a velvety polish with beeswax and vegetable oils, which emphasizes the natural grain of the wood and preserves its special feel.
Every wooden toy from Wooden Story tells a little story of the forest, naturally and safely. For the protection and enjoyment of the child (and many an adult), as the forest spirit Borowy could not have wished for better.

Even in the busy everyday life of a family, this material proves to be easy to clean (traces of use such as spills can simply be wiped off), scratch-resistant (in case the house cat is looking for a jump-off ramp) and impact-resistant (in case the offspring needs an abrupt hold).

Our CONTAINER DS has a casing made of folded sheet steel - as standard and on all sides. Too much of an edge? Or do you want a smooth shelf? The bench board offers a smooth surface for sitting or as a shelf. Can bear loads of up to 100 kilograms, suitable for the CONTAINER DS, CONTAINER DS AIR, CONTAINER DS with lock, CONTAINER DS FLAT and TARA shelving unit. The bench shelf is attached to the frame of the container or shelving unit using the connectors supplied. This allows it to be used as a place for the TV or other equipment. We recommend the seat cushion for the bench board to provide seating and more seating comfort. Max. load weight: 160 kg.
Series Container DS
Synonymous with storage and transport: the container in its archetypal surface of folded steel. We offer this cabinet furniture in the miniaturized form of overseas containers in four different versions. These well-proportioned storage boxes serve many purposes and areas of use. All containers have perforations in the bottoms for passing cables. The classic container as well as the flat and small container have doors hinged to the top of the body, which slide into the top of the body when opened and thus almost completely disappear. The CONTAINER DS PLUS is upright and has a conventional hinged door on the side.
The classic: The CONTAINER DS in the proportion of a sea container is virtually the archetype of the series CONTAINER DS. It serves as a cabinet in the living room for china and utensils for the set table, in the office for storing files in standardized format or for paper and office utensils. As a chest of drawers for linen and as a piece of furniture in the hallway and wardrobe. It can be combined in its basic rectangular shape with a variety of complementary accessories. Various feet and casters or the two framework frames serve as the basis. The shelf element TARA has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery. The coat rack completes the container to a functional wardrobe. The container of this format is available in limited color selection equipped with a lock. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The flat one: CONTAINER DS FLAT has the footprint of the classic CONTAINER DS and can be connected to it in height and stacked. It can be combined with the above mentioned accessories of the classic CONTAINER DS. This container often serves as a flat element that is built into a stack of the classic container. It is useful with its special volume for the stack of paper, for utensils and as a shelf for many purposes. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The small one: The CONTAINER DS KLEIN as the little brother of the CONTAINER DS does not have the proportions of a sea container, unlike its archetypal big role model - it is narrower, with identical depth and height. With its small size and unusual formatting, it serves as a piece of side furniture next to the bed and sofa and can also be stacked up to form a tower. It can be equipped with all separate feet as well as the casters. Unlike its sister models, it is always equipped with a smooth cover shelf in the respective color. The shelf element TARA KLEIN has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery.
The big one: A very special piece of furniture with its own range of uses is the CONTAINER DS PLUS. It can be used in portrait format and serves as a locker-like clothes or wardrobe cabinet and can also be used as a large-volume cabinet, individually or stacked on top of each other in the kitchen, office or other places. This large container is stackable like all other sister models via included square connectors. A clothes rail is included, and a specially designed shelf and cover shelf are available separately as accessories.

product_834.product_name: Hinged drawer container, sheet steel, 5-compartment Polychrom Dario
product_834.alt_text: Hinged drawer container, sheet steel, 5-compartment Polychrom Dario
product_834.description:
General Information
Exclusive
We appreciate the good things, and sometimes we want to make the good things a little better. To make the sheet steel pivot container known as the "Pivot Cabinet" accessible to lively room concepts, we have combined fresh colors based on the RAL palette to create a powerful design element of its own. The color combination of the "Dario" container with RAL 2021 water blue and RAL 6027 light green as well as RAL 2012 salmon orange and RAL 3000 fire red around the central RAL 280-2 is available exclusively from Manufactum.
Home Smart Home. Container with a future
Its design is reminiscent of the utopias of the 1960s, its construction has reached maturity, its choice of materials is more sophisticated than ever before and its functionality is as flexible as visionaries could wish for.
Called a "pivot cabinet" in English - "pivot" means something like "pivot joint" or "swivel axis" - this name refers to the essential design element of the container: the individual drawers are swung open on an axis, not pulled open or folded down as is usually the case. This design idea was made famous by Joe Colombo's "Boby" roll container developed in 1970. The Italian architect was also one of the leading futuristic industrial designers of the 1960s, a time of optimism and visions of the future, which - following Herbert Marcuse's train of thought, for example - sought to pave the way out of the realm of necessity and into the realm of freedom. Designs such as Verner Panton's cantilever "Panton Chair", Olivier Mourgue's "Djinn" armchair, which adorned the interior of the space station in "2001 - A Space Odyssey", and Colombo's "Tube Chair" became icons. Colombo's "dynamic pieces of furniture" always aimed to be multifunctional.
Our swivel drawer container builds on the ideal of those designs, but doesn't just quote the utopias of past decades, but smartly brings the future into your home today. While Colombo and his colleagues were still enthusiastic about the newly developed plastics of the 1960s, we know better today and prefer sheet steel, which offers far greater stability and durability. The sheet steel thus reinforces the versatility of the container. In the kitchen, bathroom, living room or entrance area - sturdy and stable, the hinged drawer container takes on its intended functions of storage, presentation and easy access in any environment and, like any successful design object, fulfills the role of eye-catcher in a stylish and colourful way.
Unique color combination: Dario
This vibrant combination of colors is available exclusively from Manufactum. Similar to a color wheel, it completes the arc from blue to red: at the center of the color combination is RAL 280-2, a rather soft and calm color from the RAL Effect spectrum, which mediates between the powerful hues of the upper and lower rotary drawers. Water blue and light green form the fresh, lively upper entry, while warm salmon orange and intense fire red set the lower accent.
With an undivided surface area of around A4 size, the revolving drawers can hold larger and smaller good things. The design is well thought out and solidly constructed: The front round steel, which connects the top cover and base of the container, forms the pivot axis so that the drawers are flush with the rear steel tubes when closed; with the help of a small magnet on the rear wall, they dock into place with a gentle snap. And even if they don't beep or flash to let you know that the fridge needs to be refilled, the drawers reveal all the necessary and possible contents by swiveling open 270 degrees and providing a complete overview. At the bottom, the height-adjustable feet ensure that you can counteract any unevenness in the surface. And if you also want to make your designer furniture more mobile, we offer a separate set of matching castor feet for the swivel drawer container, which you can screw into place of the feet in no time at all.
Attention:
Please observe the maximum permissible load capacity of the revolving drawers. Distribute the weight evenly. Heavier objects should be placed in the lower, lighter ones in the upper revolving drawers. Do not open more than one revolving drawer at a time to avoid tipping over. Do not leave small children unattended with this piece of furniture.
Responsible economic operator for the EU

product_838.product_name: Work and serving table Plico, rollable
product_838.alt_text: Work and serving table Plico, rollable
product_838.description:
General Information
The PLICO serving trolley designed by Richard Sapper in the 1970s is one of his lesser-known projects, although it is one of his strongest designs. His more popular designs include the TIZIO work lamp and the ZOOM BIKE, which folds to a minimal size. Sapper was a master of construction and a great lover of so-called collapsibles. These space-saving products can be folded or modified thanks to their design, making them more versatile in their application. Sapper himself declared it an essential goal of his design work to solve and eliminate problems or defects that can be identified in existing objects. PLICO is handy and extremely compact when folded. Simply grab the top shelf and pull it upwards - and the furniture folds up. When folded, PLICO takes up minimal space and can be placed behind the kitchen door or between two pieces of kitchen furniture, for example, and remains stable thanks to the brakes on the rear wheels. It can be used in a variety of ways, as a serving trolley, as a side table by the bed or sofa or as a small, extremely flexible work table where you want to sit with your laptop and also need shelves for this and that work utensil. The top surface can be folded down in one simple movement, completely changing the structure of the trolley. The shelf now protrudes slightly above the trolley and serves as a usable surface. The structure of the serving trolley is made of black lacquered steel. The shelves are made of matt black lacquered thermoplastic resin, a very high-quality and durable plastic. Four rubber-coated castors, two of which can be steered and two of which have locking brakes, also glide over textile floors. Max. load weight: lower shelf: 7 kg, upper shelf: 4 kg or 12 kg.

General Information
Discover MAGAZIN products: Collaborating with innovative designers, MAGAZIN develops and produces this unique furniture and home accessories series.
Small occasional unit and pedestal from the HENRY series - at its lowest height, it can be used as a companion next to the desk, as a small bedside table and in many other places in the living or working space. Max. load weight: 80 kg.
Container Henry
A shelving tower with multiple uses: HENRY in small, medium and large is an object-like focal point in the room or discreet furniture. HENRY stands freely, independently and accessible from all sides as a room divider or as a complementary piece of furniture in the bathroom, living room or hallway. Easy to move on freely rotating, concealed castors. A shelf insert and a drawer - both made of sheet steel - complement HENRY and extend its function. We strive for this variety of applications in all our MAGAZIN products. In addition to its functionality, this small piece of furniture impresses with its ingenious design: panels milled at a 45-degree angle interlock at different heights. This gives HENRY a very fine contour and at the same time emphasizes the high-quality material, whose plywood core is thus visible. HENRY comes fully assembled. We discovered HENRY and the designers from Studio Sergeant, led by the young Belgian Pieter van den Poel, at an exhibition of graduates from the "Thomas More Hogeschool Mechelen". With the name of their piece of furniture, the young designers want to commemorate the architect Henry van der Velde, who left his home town of Ghent a striking book tower with the architecture of the "Boekentoren" library building.

General Information
Stored within easy reach on the desk bookcase
Standing books tend to tip over, stacks of books tend to slip. Keeping books in place by storing or transporting them on a shelf that is tilted backwards rather than using side supports has long been a tried and tested practice in libraries here, as our book trolley documents. In contrast, the small piece of furniture known in the USA as the "desktop bookshelf", which uses the design feature of the inclined shelf for the handset, is still not very widespread. Frequently used books, reference books, notebooks or address books can be stored there. This bookshelf provides the reader with an appropriate service at their preferred reading place - for example on the desk or bedside table - and, with a usable width of 38 cm, holds not only current but also future reading. Nevertheless, it saves enough space so that it doesn't take up the whole desk and can be quickly put to one side if necessary thanks to its handy format. The powder-coated sheet steel version is in no way inferior to the oak desk bookcase, which we have had in our range for some time, in terms of appearance and quality - despite its lower price. The small piece of furniture from Schwerte, whose metal sheets are folded and spot-welded - without any unpleasant sharp edges - does not need any feet: The relatively wide, powder-coated and therefore slightly rough base ensures a good grip on the table.

product_850.description:
General Information
Exclusive
There is nothing that can not be done a little better, even with this in itself quite durable toilet brush. For us, the manufacturer makes it with a handle made of larch wood, which can tolerate moisture very well and withstands the demands of the bathroom or sauna perfectly.
Not bristly at all. Toilet brush with fins
At first glance, it appears to be a classic toilet brush, but what sets it apart is the bristles. The Loowy toilet brush is not equipped with bristles, but with flaps made of thermoplastic rubber. And this has several advantages. Thanks to the robust material and corrugated shape, the flaps have an excellent cleaning performance. They last up to five times longer than normal bristles and maintain their cleaning power right to the end. The material surface is water-repellent - and although it does not have a real lotus effect, everything rolls off so that you can put the toilet brush back in the ceramic holder without dripping. This also makes the material easy to clean - thanks to the lamellar shape, hardly anything sticks to it anyway.
But durable
What we like even more, however, is that the toilet brush is very durable. Its sturdy handle is made for us from larch wood, which is resistant to moisture and is therefore often used for bathroom and sauna accessories, garden furniture or other utensils that are left outside. A robust connection system holds the handle and slat head together. The latter is replaceable (you can also find replacements from us), but this is rarely necessary. This reduces the burden on the environment twice over. If you also remember to use the economy button on the toilet flush, you can save a lot in the bathroom. The toilet brush is supplied with a quiver made of Westerwald clay. Both are made entirely in Germany.

product_851.description:
General Information
For sorting, storing and carrying. Basket made from Milulu grass
Mifuko is Swahili and means bag. The collaboration between Finnish designer duo Minna Impiö and Mari Martikainen and Kenyan women also began with bags and baskets - so what could be more natural than to name their company the same? The Mifuko range includes products that are made by hand from resource-saving or renewable natural materials. The focus is on bags and baskets made from regional materials such as sisal, milulu grass, palm leaves, elephant grass or paper cords, but recycled plastic is also used. The containers are not only intended for transport purposes, but primarily as versatile storage and organization aids in the home, such as this large basket made from robust Milulu grass (Eleocharis acutangula), a reed-like species of marsh rush that grows in tropical wetlands. The milulu grass for this basket comes from Tanzania and is also processed there, in the village of Iringa, using the traditional weaving technique. The Milulu grass basket is stiffer than the Mifuko sisal basket. Due to its openwork weave, it ensures excellent air circulation, which makes it ideal as a laundry basket. It can be used just as well for storing toys, blankets, newspapers or magazines and much more. Thanks to the sturdy leather carrying straps, you can carry the Milulu basket comfortably even when full. You can see who wove your basket on the attached sign, where the women sign their names.
Mifuko - Kenyan tradition in Finnish designs
Kenyan tradition and craftsmanship characterize the designs of the Finnish label Mifuko. The long-standing connection with Kenya enabled the two designers Minna Impiö and Mari Martikainen to start a cooperation with Kenyan craftswomen in 2009 so that the products could also be manufactured in Kenya. Mifuko now works with around 400 women, not only in Kenya, but also in Tanzania, Ethiopia and Ghana. They live mainly in rural areas and work primarily in agriculture. In the dry season, they weave carpets, weave baskets or bags, make jewelry and many other decorative items. Fair payment and long-term business relationships are just as important as the skills and traditional manufacturing techniques are taken into account when designing the products. This gives the women the opportunity to expand their knowledge and pass it on to younger women. They can build up their own network and are ultimately able to earn an additional income, as the women and their families primarily work in agriculture. Only when their own fields have been cultivated and the animals cared for do they produce for Mifuko, thus earning an additional income that often saves them during the drought.
Mifuko is a member of the World Fair Trade Organization (WFTO). On the one hand, this implies the permanent implementation and monitoring of fair trade and fair pay, and on the other hand, care is taken to ensure that the natural habitat is affected as little as possible during the manufacture of the products and that occupational safety is guaranteed. In addition, Minna Impiö and Mari Martikainen finance projects that improve the lives of the workers and their families, such as the construction of sanitary facilities.
Note:
Certain manufacturing steps are carried out by hand. Slight dimensional and color deviations may therefore occur.

product_856.description:
General Information
Gentle splashing, fragrance and steam
Gentle splashing, constant fragrance - with this small springbrunnen you can create a relaxing atmosphere in the sauna (completely without electricity). It comes, how could it be otherwise, from the land of sauna-goers, where it is made by hand from soapstone. Thanks to the heat-retaining material, it works solely through the sauna heat: the soapstone transfers the absorbed heat to the water, which evaporates and constantly humidifies the air. Traditionally, the Springbrunnen is only filled with water; by adding fragrant sauna additives or essential oils, their fine aroma is distributed in the sauna with the steam.
The gentle splashing of the small water fountains is particularly soothing. These are created when some of the water in the tubes heats up to boiling point, whereupon it suddenly evaporates and is expelled. Due to the resulting negative pressure in the tube, water is sucked in again, heated, ejected ... With the first water filling, the Sauna-Springbrunnen initially bubbles softly. When you add water, strong columns of springbrunnenwater form. The Springbrunnen bubbles most strongly during this initial phase (therefore be particularly careful when filling the Brunnenbasin for the first time). The bubbling becomes more even with each refill. However, you can also influence the Springbrunneneffect by its position on the heat source: the hotter the Brunnen is, the more the water bubbles.
Caution:
Never try to change the position of the Springbrunnens while the furnace is hot.
Be extra careful when filling for the first time!
Do not let children play with the Brunnen unsupervised!

product_857.description:
General Information
Multiple benefits
Spacious catch basin for discarded desk papers, used towels or even the knitting next to the couch: this basket impresses with its versatile use, its natural materiality and, last but not least, its extremely attractive appearance. Even purists who think in terms of material economy will get their money's worth here, because despite its visual and functional opulence, the design of this paper and laundry basket impresses with its well thought-out minimalism. A three-layer thick veneer sheet is bent to form an almost cylindrical body, interlocked to maintain its shape and glued to the circular base plate; the upper edge is reinforced by an inner ring made of three-layer wood. Covered with a fine layer of clear varnish so that the individual grain stands out even more beautifully, the result is a stable lightweight that can be carried around effortlessly using the two side handles - if you don't want to take your eyes off this simple beauty (or simply want to transport the towels to the washing machine).
Tradition x modernity. Mint Furniture
Anyone who still thinks that traditional craftsmanship results in furniture à la Gelsenkirchen Baroque should turn their gaze to Riga. There, the company Mint Furniture, founded in 2009, stands for furniture design in which the tried and tested is taken up and further developed in form and function. This is the essence of innovation anyway, especially when it wants to stand out from the mass of supposed modernity in a visionary way. The team at Mint Furniture, which combines knowledge of fine art, interior design, industrial design and craftsmanship, has also achieved something astonishing: an individual design signature that is revealed in the fine details. With his spindle stool made of solid oak, co-founder Janis Rauza laid the foundation for the creative combination of formal tradition and functional modernity. Continuously expanded, the entire furniture collection from Mint Furniture follows this vision: expertly crafted by cabinetmakers, supported by a profound knowledge of the possibilities of the material and supported by the use of modern technologies, the designs point far into the future as pieces for generations.

product_867.description:
General Information
A Tisket, a Tasket, a Children’s Wicker Basket.
We’ve offered large wicker baskets like this one for several years. The same manufacturer in Franconia produces a smaller version for children, which is also popular with adults. The children’s wicker basket, like the larger version, is made with a technique providing highly stable basket with smooth, clean surfaces inside and out. The basket is equipped with two wooden skids underneath: a traditional way to protect the floor known from rustic furniture. Starting from the bottom, the weaver constitutes a perfect rectangle and inserts along all four sides the willow cuttings. The manufacturer is a fourth generation master workshop and one of the last today that trains apprentices in this work intensive manufacturing technique, bringing a traditional craftsmanship back to life.
Incomparable quality. Wicker basket in cube technique: made in Franconia.
This laundry basket has little in common with its - significantly cheaper - competitors, which are hawked by flying merchants up and down the country. Good laundry baskets were already made in this way more than 100 years ago: in the so-called cube technique, i.e. with a double-walled wickerwork, which on the one hand ensures a very high stability and on the other hand a smooth surface on the inside as well as on the outside. On the underside, as has always been the case with such traditionally crafted utility baskets, the basket is equipped with smoothly polished wooden runners to protect the bottom. The construction of the basket begins with the bottom, into which beams are inserted all around. Bent upwards, the beams form a framework that is woven out using the cube technique. The workpieces are made freehand without a mold. Our manufacturer is a fourth-generation master craftsman and one of the last to produce and train in this time-consuming and therefore cost-intensive method. But baskets of this type are not only solid: in case of emergency (which rarely happens) they can be repaired, unlike their plastic counterparts.
For the big and the small laundry. For big and small
The wicker basket is available in two sizes: a large one for laundry and a small one that can be used by children, but is just as appealing to adults. The children's wicker basket is made of the same material and just as elaborately as the large one.

Temperature and humidity at a glance
Knowing the exact temperature and humidity is literally elementary for a pleasant and safe sauna session. It therefore makes sense to combine both measuring devices in one instrument so that the required information can be read at a glance. This simple but effective steam stone, which is called "Höyrykivet" in Finland, comes from the land of sauna enthusiasts. product_891.description:
General Information
Double occupancy. Extra wide brass towel rack
This towel holder is manufactured in the Giese manufactory in Sauerland, which is still family-run today. 100 years of experience in working with metals goes into the manufacturing process. Two solid brass rods are soldered to the holders by hand, excess brass solder is ground off, and the edges and transitions are carefully smoothed and polished. Finally, the metal is coated with a layer of chrome that protects against moisture and corrosion - wear and tear is virtually eliminated.
With a width of 70 cm, the towel holder is so generously dimensioned that there is also room for bath towels on it. In addition, very practical: the holder can be fixed as usual by dowels and screws, but there are also two sets for adhesive mounting, so that the tiles do not have to be drilled. When moving or remodeling the bathroom, the adhesive residue can be completely removed and the holder can be attached elsewhere using separately ordered adhesive sets.
High strength adhesive mounting. Undamaged tiles
Drilled tiles are always a nuisance, especially if a wall-mounted hook or holder should or must be subsequently relocated. We put an end to this annoyance by supplying the product not only with the conventional screw-on technique, but also with an additional set for adhesive mounting. The enclosed fast-curing adhesive is characterized by its high adhesive strength and can still be removed without residue if necessary.
Chrome-plated brass in the bathroom
Everything is chrome-plated these days: the thinnest steel sheets, die-cast zinc and even plastic. You can usually tell by the weight. However, chrome plating is often poor and inadequate. You notice it - usually too late - when the wafer-thin layer of chrome peels off after a few weeks and the metal underneath starts to rust or react. (There are chrome-plated steel appliances on which, for example, a natural sponge will turn brown within a few days). Under the chrome layer of our Giese appliances, however, is solid and additionally nickel-plated brass. So you can be sure that these items are durable and will not rust.

General Information
Ascetic: bathroom utensil comprised of a ring and a rod.
These utensils, designed by architect Theo Keller, are manufactured in a southern German metalworking shop with a great deal of technical precision. The principle: all utensils – from towel rod, to soap holder, to toilet paper holder - are produced by bending, snapping and rotating the same workpiece, a stainless steel rod with a diameter of 8 mm. product_913.description:
General Information
For coats or towels
This swivel hook made of polished aluminum is simply classified by the manufacturer as a triple coat hook. It is only suitable for underneath mounting - under the hat shelf in the hallway perhaps or under the kitchen worktop. Instead of coats and jackets, the lightweight hook can also hold tea towels and oven mitts as required. We source it from Hermann Schwerter in Iserlohn, a hardware dealer since 1905 and today one of the last remaining producers of fittings and coat racks in the region, which was once famous for its metalworking tradition.
Utility and Adornment. Furniture Fittings.
Historically, fittings were primarily intended to increase the usability of a piece of furniture; the focal point of their assessment was their practical use. Shields protected drawers, latches, corners, and edges against wear and tear in particularly stressed areas. All door knobs and drawer handles had to be particularly sturdy. The awareness of an ornamental value of such objects, on the other hand, came about later and only over the course of centuries. From the 12th century onwards, you find fittings that had a style-defining effect on their era. The Art Nouveau phase was particularly productive, creating a multitude of dainty floral décor ornaments.
European Diversity. Our Selection.
Nevertheless, the emphasis in our assortment is on the material as well as the origin of the individual articles. The century from which the design originates is less important to us. You won’t find cheap imitations from India and China in our selection; on the contrary, you will find products originating in Europe – with an emphasis on regions where the production of such fittings was traditionally at home. For example, the glass furniture knobs in our range come from a specialised glassmaking workshop in the Fichtel Mountains. One and all of our porcelain products derive from the cradle of French porcelain production, from the city of Limoges. And an iron foundry in the Ardennes provides us with the iron teacup handles. Last but not least, we have our pick’s brass furniture plates and handles made in Lüdenscheid in the Sauerland region, a traditional centre of metalworking in Germany.
Your Design Options.
You can use the fittings to embellish old furnishings or replace existing, possibly defective parts with functioning ones. Upgrade the long-cherished flea market find in a heartbeat. Deck out a self-made piece of furniture with the fittings it deserves: smooth-running castors and charming handles.

product_920.description:
General Information
More than a beautiful appearance. Alternative wax
They burn evenly and with that special soft glow that is characteristic of a tea light. At first glance, these tea lights are no different from their commercially available siblings. However, in this case, the appearance is not only beautiful, but also very deceptive - in the best sense of the word: the eco tea lights are made from a special biomass. Completely free of petroleum-based kerosene, they consist of 100 percent recycled residual fats and oils from the food industry, gastronomy and the hotel industry.
Biokema. Effectively innovative
In the interests of conserving resources, no fresh oilseeds such as rapeseed, palm or soybean oil are used for the eco tea lights, which are (yet to be) used for food. Although these may come from organic farming, their large-scale cultivation endangers natural biodiversity. And as the oilseeds often have to be imported, the transportation routes of the product would be longer.
However, the careful use of natural resources, the protection of biodiversity and the preservation of ecosystems is the declared aim of the Thuringian company LipiTec, which has developed an innovative option for cascade use. In a patented process, waste fats and oils from the food industry are carefully purified and recycled into a biomass that can be used to produce candles, among other things. Sold under the brand name Biokema, these candles are an impressive example of how recycling can increase raw material efficiency.
Note
Due to the manufacturing process, the eco tea lights initially have a slightly crumbly consistency. However, once they are lit, the biomass heats up and solidifies evenly - the candles burn evenly, with little soot and odor. We recommend the use of stainless steel tea light holders.

General Information
In The Forest
Brings the olfactory sensuality of the forest into your home: the subtle freshness of spruce needles combines with woody cedar notes to create a naturally warm fragrance.
Coudre Berlin. From a single mold
"Coudre" means "to sew". When it comes to scented candles, the name of the Berlin label may be confusing, but before the scented candles came fashion, or more precisely: a new menswear collection. It all began in 2016, when Berliners Dimitri Moustakidis and Daniel Diederich had just launched their first collection of timeless basics and were now looking for ways to add an atmospheric touch to their creations. After all, fashion is not just a piece of fabric on the body; clothing also reflects a mood. Fashion and mood from a single source: the two designers finally decided on candles that would capture an atmosphere olfactorily and inspire at the same time. Moustakidis and Diederich developed their first fragrance compositions in a small kitchen in Prenzlauer Berg - with the aim of using only natural raw materials and ingredients. Once they had found a scent that appealed to them, they captured it in the candles - and poured each individual candle by hand.
Little by little, a whole series of scented candles was created. Despite the success of their creations and compositions, Coudre Berlin continues to attach great importance to meticulous craftsmanship. Each scented candle is still poured by hand in a Berlin workshop and only natural ingredients are used. The vegetable wax is made from sunflower and olive oil, while the olfactory ingredient is pure essential oils. Practical additional benefit: The scented candles are poured into brewing jars with Bakelite® screw-on lids. Once all wax residue has been removed and thoroughly cleaned, the jars can be reused as storage containers.
Note:
When burning the candle for the first time, please allow it to burn until the entire surface has liquefied. Only then will the fragrance molecules dissolve completely and the fragrance can unfold optimally. This also prevents a funnel and ultimately a tunnel from forming in the wax. To extinguish the flame, simply dip the wick briefly into the wax with a match and put it back in place. This prevents soot from forming and the candle burns well again. The next time you light the candle, make sure that the wick is not too long; it is best to shorten it regularly to 0.5 centimeters. Wax residue on the glass wall can be liquefied by briefly placing the glass in the oven at 60 °C. If you wish to continue using the jar, please remove any wax residue and clean the jar with hot water and washing-up liquid.

Mountain air: forest-fresh scent of Swiss stone pine needles, juniper branches and lemon peel, reminiscent of a hike in the mountains. Aromatherapy effect: helps to clear the head, strengthen and balance.
Nature in a candle. Smells good and does you good
Bring the scent of nature indoors? These candles can do just that: whether spicy forest air with a tangy Swiss stone pine aroma (mountain air), spicy lavender scent with juniper (leisure time) or rosemary notes (homecoming) or fruity orange and lemon notes with warm cinnamon and vanilla aromas (evening gold). Many find the fragrances soothingly relaxing or pleasantly invigorating, depending on the aroma. In these candles, the well-composed blends of exclusively natural essential plant oils provide the intense fragrance. The candle wax is also obtained from purely plant-based raw materials (from rapeseed and soy) - so you can breathe deeply and relax twice as much. And for a long time, because the vegetable wax burns significantly longer than mineral oil-based wax. Once the scented candle has burned down, you can use the decorative jar for a variety of purposes, as it comes with a lid made from certified, dark-stained oak wood. Another practical feature is that it can be used as a saucer for the burning scented candle, protecting the base from heat. Half of the smoked glass is made from recycled glass.
Looops has given its scented candles a new look and, in some cases, a new name. If you are already familiar with the candles and would now like to buy the fireplace whisper, choose the Homecoming scented candle, the feel-good time has turned into leisure time.

In the mountains, they say, the mind is free. It was in the mountains, more precisely in the Salzkammergut on the northern edge of the Alps, that Julia Schliefsteiner and Markus Niederfriniger came up with the idea of their own fragrancekerzen-Manufaktur to capture and preserve the scents of nature and take them home with them. The fire was lit: they founded Looops Kerzenmanuaktur, and the deeper they delved into the world of fragrances and aromas, the more they realized how far-reaching their effects could be and that the findings of aromatherapy could be wonderfully combined with their new craft. So Julia Schliefsteiner went straight on to complete her aromatherapy training and is now very familiar with the gentle extraction of essential oils and their effects.
Nature as inspiration and source
True to their principle "Nature is good the way it is", they add neither artificial nor synthetic substances and use vegetable wax obtained from rapidly renewable plants (soy and rapeseed) - which also has the advantage that these plant-based candles burn longer and produce less soot than mineral oil-based ones. The wicks are made of pure cotton or even wood. Julia Schliefsteiner creates all the fragrances herself in the company's own "kitchen" near Salzburg. The scented candles are also made by hand there - a complex process involving many steps. It begins with the extraction of the valuable, fragrant and highly effective oils from herbs, flowers and fruits. For new creations, the mixtures of essential oils are first left to rest for a while so that the various fragrance components can blend into a single unit. Only then are small test candles poured and the fragrances tested over several days. The creations are usually inspired by the landscape of the Salzkammergut, the herbs on the mountain pasture or the forest shortly after the rain. After all, a hike through the mountains and nature not only clears the mind, but also fills it with new ideas.

General Information
Swedish light. Candlelight without dripping.
The Kanalljus comes from Liljeholmens in Sweden, where quality candles have been produced since 1839. The candle is made purely from stearin of animal origin - i.e. without palm oil. There are four channels around the wick into which (excess) liquid wax flows. The effect: the candle burns with majestic calm and its large, bright flame gives off a regal light, producing hardly any soot. Originally, such channel candles were developed for use in churches: The constant draught there considerably increases the dripping of simple candles, whereas the channel candle hardly causes even strong draughts to flicker and drip. The relatively high melting point of stearin allows the candle to burn with a sharp, even edge. At the same time, it makes the candle dimensionally stable; even high ambient temperatures do not cause it to bend. After extinguishing, the liquid wax solidifies very quickly and the wick does not continue to glow.

Panier des Sens created their first perfumes in Sault, a small village in the Vaucluse region, surrounded by lush lavender fields – some claim they are the most beautiful in Provence. The Mediterranean Sea, landscape, and flora contribute to the family-owned company’s inspiration for creating fragrances. The scents are fresh creations of uncomplicated and light character, made from natural extracts and essential oils sourced from the region. The formulations come from Perfumers in Grasse, and Panier des Sens produces its scents in the tradition-steeped town near the French Riviera according to the classical artistry of perfumery.
Note:
When burning the candle for the first time, please allow it to burn until the entire surface has liquefied. Only then will the fragrance molecules dissolve completely and the fragrance can unfold optimally. This also prevents a funnel and ultimately a tunnel from forming in the wax. To extinguish the flame, simply dip the wick briefly into the wax with a match and put it back in place. This prevents soot from forming and the candle burns well again. The next time you light the candle, make sure that the wick is not too long; it is best to shorten it regularly to 0.5 centimeters. Wax residue on the glass wall can be liquefied by briefly placing the glass in the oven at 60 °C. If you wish to continue using the jar, please remove any wax residue and clean the jar with hot water and washing-up liquid.

product_932.description:
General Information
Rediscovered crop. Rapeseed
If you travel to Schleswig-Holstein in April and May, you will pass many yellow rapeseed fields, which set the wide, hilly landscape in a particularly beautiful light. Rapeseed has always been one of the most important sources of oil here, but is also important for crop rotation in agriculture, partly because it can break chains of infection in cereal diseases. While rapeseed oil was primarily used for lamp oil or lubricating oil for industry and soap production until the middle of the 19th century, it was soon replaced by cheap petroleum-based fuels and edible oils from overseas. It is only since the 1970s that rapeseed oil can also be used as cooking oil and animal feed, thanks to new varieties that contain almost no bitter erucic acid. Since then, the area under cultivation has been steadily increasing and the possible uses have also been further developed.
Fragrant rapeseed candles
The Itzehoer candle manufacturer produces these scented candles on the basis of rapeseed oil. This not only has the advantage of being a regional, renewable raw material that can be procured via short transportation routes, but the candles are also purely plant-based and completely free of harmful substances. Rapeseed wax is also very suitable as a carrier for scented oils, which are initially safely enclosed in the wax and only develop their full aroma when the candle burns. In this case, it is pure essential oils that give the candles their pleasant fragrance. They come with a candle holder in the shape of a classic Weck® jar with a lid - and are therefore ready for immediate use.

General Information
They Last a Long Time and Will Illuminate Even the Remotest Corner.
These well-conceived tea lights have three key features. First of all, the source of light: the candles are made in a Franconian candle factory; they are taller than usual hence they burn longer and the actual combustion proceeds without mishaps. Secondly, the cup is made of ribbed moulded glass: it can always be refilled and when the candle burns low the light shines through the wall of the cup, creating a lovely pattern. And thirdly, the durable tin lid: it extinguishes the flame and keeps the tea light clean and free of dust when not in use.
Tradition of efficiency. Glafey
Glafey in Nuremberg is a proven expert in the field of candles with wick holders. Thanks to operating experience dating back to 1808, these candles are functionally perfected: they burn with little soot, are odorless and produce exactly the right amount of light for a long burning time. The wick and wick wax are also precisely matched to these requirements.
During production, care has always been taken to use raw materials efficiently and sparingly. For example, the tealights, which have been produced unchanged for decades and whose pack of 12 uses just one tinplate bowl that can be refilled again and again - the refill pack is supplied without a bowl. Or the cork floats and wicks, which have been produced since 1867 (and are only available separately from us), which can be made into fully-fledged oil lights with minimal use of materials and "on-board resources" (glass jar and vegetable oil).
Glafey also relies on plastic-free outer packaging made from cardboard and glassine. In production, Glafey obtains heat from a combined heat and power plant, in which the fuels used are converted particularly efficiently into usable energy, and electricity from 3,000 square meters of solar modules on the company's own roof - which means that one of the oldest light sources is produced under the most modern conditions.

General Information
Fine accent. Subtle fragrance
The classic beehive, also known by beekeepers as a "hive" or "inverted hive", is a development of humans, not honey bees. Wild bees do not need such dwellings; most species do not even form colonies, but live solitary lives. They colonize cavities in the ground or in walls and rocks, between dead wood or in stems, tree trunks and the like. However, the hive of a honey bee colony cared for by a beekeeper has become so engrained in the collective imagination that the beehive is inevitably associated with every bee colony collecting nectar and pollen.
The beehive candle is an aesthetic reminiscence of the honey bee and its industrious service to mankind. Hand-cast in a North German candle manufactory, this "hive" also exudes the subtle scent of summer blossom and honey as a purely decorative element and adds a subtle accent to your creative interior design. When you light the candle, it spreads its warm light for many hours. (If, on the other hand, you are - at least inwardly - in favor of a fireless arrangement with some bees: You can also find these in our range, felted by hand from pure new wool and as durable as the unlit candle).

General Information
Homecoming: With fine, spicy herbal scent of rosemary, lavender and clove. Aromatherapy effect: decelerates, warms, harmonizing energy.
Looops scented candles for refilling
Looops has developed the scented candles in this format with paper cup especially for refilling the jars with wooden lids. This means you can use the jars for a long time. As the wax is purely vegetable, it can be easily washed off the jars with hot water and a little washing-up liquid. Please note that the candles must not be lit in the paper cup, as it is not fireproof and does not stand securely. To make it easier to remove the candles, place the cup in the freezer for about an hour: the wax will then separate better from the cup wall. The four fragrances available are Mountain Air, Leisure Time, Homecoming and Evening Gold.
Capture fragrances. Bringing nature home
In the mountains, they say, the mind is free. It was in the mountains, more precisely in the Salzkammergut on the northern edge of the Alps, that Julia Schliefsteiner and Markus Niederfriniger came up with the idea of their own fragrancekerzen-Manufaktur to capture and preserve the scents of nature and take them home with them. The fire was lit: they founded Looops Kerzenmanuaktur, and the deeper they delved into the world of fragrances and aromas, the more they realized how far-reaching their effects could be and that the findings of aromatherapy could be wonderfully combined with their new craft. So Julia Schliefsteiner went straight on to complete her aromatherapy training and is now very familiar with the gentle extraction of essential oils and their effects.
Nature as inspiration and source
True to their principle "Nature is good the way it is", they add neither artificial nor synthetic substances and use vegetable wax obtained from rapidly renewable plants (soy and rapeseed) - which also has the advantage that these plant-based candles burn longer and produce less soot than mineral oil-based ones. The wicks are made of pure cotton or even wood. Julia Schliefsteiner creates all the fragrances herself in the company's own "kitchen" near Salzburg. The scented candles are also made by hand there - a complex process involving many steps. It begins with the extraction of the valuable, fragrant and highly effective oils from herbs, flowers and fruits. For new creations, the mixtures of essential oils are first left to rest for a while so that the various fragrance components can blend into a single unit. Only then are small test candles poured and the fragrances tested over several days. The creations are usually inspired by the landscape of the Salzkammergut, the herbs on the mountain pasture or the forest shortly after the rain. After all, a hike through the mountains and nature not only clears the mind, but also fills it with new ideas.

For Those Who Want to Fly High: Secure Wall Fixing.
This universally usable wall fixing kit consists of two wire ropes laid in loops and two ring bolts with dowels. We recommend using the securing device as soon as assembled shelving systems exceed a height of 160 centimetres. The UNIVERSAL WALL FIXING KIT is compatible with various shelving systems.
Series Container DS
Synonymous with storage and transport: the container in its archetypal surface of folded steel. We offer this cabinet furniture in the miniaturized form of overseas containers in four different versions. These well-proportioned storage boxes serve many purposes and areas of use. All containers have perforations in the bottoms for passing cables. The classic container as well as the flat and small container have doors hinged to the top of the body, which slide into the top of the body when opened and thus almost completely disappear. The CONTAINER DS PLUS is upright and has a conventional hinged door on the side.
The classic: The CONTAINER DS in the proportion of a sea container is virtually the archetype of the series CONTAINER DS. It serves as a cabinet in the living room for china and utensils for the set table, in the office for storing files in standardized format or for paper and office utensils. As a chest of drawers for linen and as a piece of furniture in the hallway and wardrobe. It can be combined in its basic rectangular shape with a variety of complementary accessories. Various feet and casters or the two framework frames serve as the basis. The shelf element TARA has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery. The coat rack completes the container to a functional wardrobe. The container of this format is available in limited color selection equipped with a lock. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The flat one: CONTAINER DS FLAT has the footprint of the classic CONTAINER DS and can be connected to it in height and stacked. It can be combined with the above mentioned accessories of the classic CONTAINER DS. This container often serves as a flat element that is built into a stack of the classic container. It is useful with its special volume for the stack of paper, for utensils and as a shelf for many purposes. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The small one: The CONTAINER DS KLEIN as the little brother of the CONTAINER DS does not have the proportions of a sea container, unlike its archetypal big role model - it is narrower, with identical depth and height. With its small size and unusual formatting, it serves as a piece of side furniture next to the bed and sofa and can also be stacked up to form a tower. It can be equipped with all separate feet as well as the casters. Unlike its sister models, it is always equipped with a smooth cover shelf in the respective color. The shelf element TARA KLEIN has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery.
The big one: A very special piece of furniture with its own range of uses is the CONTAINER DS PLUS. It can be used in portrait format and serves as a locker-like clothes or wardrobe cabinet and can also be used as a large-volume cabinet, individually or stacked on top of each other in the kitchen, office or other places. This large container is stackable like all other sister models via included square connectors. A clothes rail is included, and a specially designed shelf and cover shelf are available separately as accessories.

product_943.description:
General Information
Home Smart Home. Container with a future
Its design is reminiscent of the utopias of the 1960s, its construction has reached maturity, its choice of materials is more sophisticated than ever before and its functionality is as flexible as visionaries could wish for.
Called a "pivot cabinet" in English, this name - "pivot" means "pivot joint" or "swivel axis" - refers to the essential design element of the container: the individual drawers are swung open on an axis, not pulled open or folded down as is usually the case. This design idea was made famous by Joe Colombo's "Boby" roll container developed in 1970. The Italian architect was also one of the leading futuristic industrial designers of the 1960s, a time of optimism and visions of the future, which - following Herbert Marcuse's train of thought, for example - sought to pave the way out of the realm of necessity and into the realm of freedom. Designs such as Verner Panton's cantilever "Panton Chair", Olivier Mourgue's "Djinn" armchair, which adorned the interior of "2001 - A Space Odyssey", and Colombo's "Tube Chair" became icons. Colombo's "dynamic pieces of furniture" always aimed to be multifunctional.
Our swivel drawer container builds on the ideal of those designs, but doesn't just quote the utopias of past decades, but smartly brings the future into your home today. While Colombo and his colleagues were still enthusiastic about the newly developed plastics of the 1960s, we know better today and prefer sheet steel, which offers far greater stability and durability. The sheet steel thus reinforces the versatility of the container. In the kitchen, bathroom, living room or entrance area - sturdy and stable, the hinged drawer container performs its intended functions of storage, presentation and easy access in any environment and, like any successful design object, catches the eye perfectly without imposing itself on the other furniture.
With an undivided surface area of around A4, the revolving drawers can hold larger and smaller good things. The construction is well thought out and solid: The front round steel, which connects the top cover and base of the container, forms the swivel axis so that the drawers are flush with the rear steel tubes when closed; with the help of a small magnet on the rear wall, they dock into place with a gentle snap. And even if they don't beep or flash to let you know that the fridge needs to be refilled, the drawers reveal all the necessary and possible contents by swiveling open 270 degrees and providing a complete overview. At the bottom, the height-adjustable feet ensure that you can counteract any unevenness in the surface. And if you want to make your designer furniture even more mobile, we offer a separate set of castor feet for the swivel drawer container, which you can screw into place of the feet in no time at all.

Please observe the maximum permissible load capacity of the revolving drawers. Distribute the weight evenly. Heavier objects should be placed in the lower, lighter ones in the upper revolving drawers. Do not open more than one revolving drawer at a time to avoid tipping over. Do not leave small children unattended with this piece of furniture.

Compact, functional, versatile. Oak laundry chest
This laundry chest is an unmistakable relative of the Form & Refine chest bench. With its slim upright format, it is suitable for the bathroom, hallway and checkroom as well as the bedroom or dressing room, where it can be used to store laundry, cushions and blankets. In the children's room, it serves as a collection point for soft toys, building blocks etc. and even in the kitchen or living room, it cuts a fine figure as a mini sideboard or bar. Handles on the right and left make transportation easier and also ensure that the interior is ventilated.
Form & Refine. Danish design
Form & Refine is a Danish design label founded in 2018 by Helle Herman Mortensen, Jonas Herman Pedersen and Lasse Lund Lauridsen. It exemplarily follows the Scandinavian design tradition and continues it at the same time. A central point is the harmonious combination of aesthetics, function and material. The designs are clear and restrained, function leads to form and the pure materials, which are allowed to retain their original visual details and forms, are processed with perfect craftsmanship. product_950.description:
General Information
A filigree record stand in which your vinyl selection for the evening is presented discreetly, yet clearly visible. An innovative Manufactum product design - developed by us for you.
Great records, fine collection
If you own records and listen to them regularly, your heart will probably skip a beat and go into a joyful extrasystole. Because this record stand closes a gap that until now has mostly had to be filled by improvised constructions. It looks almost like a lounge chair for records, but is a veritable storage container and (presentation) frame in one. The compact and filigree frame holds around 25 to 30 records, which - just like in a record store - are displayed with the cover facing forwards. This means that the record stand always shows what is currently spinning on the platter. This is not only of interest to the listeners or guests who want to know more about the hosts' choice of music. It also does justice to the special editions with art prints, which are thus discreetly staged without being damaged themselves (at the same time, the whole thing could easily pass as a sculptural co-production). The collection in the record stand can serve as a reference folder or playlist for the evening or the week, or as a chronicle of what you have already listened to. For those with a large record collection, it can be used as a kind of hand organizer; for others, it may fit the collection itself.
Careful craftsmanship for careful handling
This record stand is made with the same care that record collectors take with their good pieces. The two frames and the base are made from natural oak wood. It is neither oiled nor waxed so that the record sleeves can safely come into contact with the wood. The strip that serves as a support surface and also connects the two leaves is also flattened to a width of two centimetres at the top. A nice detail: the individual parts of the frames are mitred and joined together by visibly glued solid wood springs, which creates a nice material contrast: longitudinal wood meets end wood. The record stand is delivered to your home in three parts, so you will have to do a little work yourself before you entrust it with your choice of records, but you can then be all the more certain that the delicate frame will hold the weight of the vinyl securely.
The record stand is manufactured in a workshop on the edge of the Ore Mountains, which primarily uses local woods. The oak wood remains untreated and is simply sanded to a velvety smooth finish so that it can develop an individual patina over time. However, you can also treat the wood surface with a wood care product to protect it against discoloration and dirt.
Innovative. Manufactum product design
Creating "living products" - i.e. products that integrate into your life, enrich your everyday life and are allowed to age with dignity - is a goal that is close to the heart of our product designer Markus Stallberg. The focus of his designs is therefore on the innovative added value that a product offers you - and the innovation consists of solving a problem that arises in our everyday lives.
"You don't stumble across good ideas," emphasizes Markus Stallberg. Rather, he approaches the solution to such an everyday problem in many small steps, the direction of which is determined by constant observation and questioning. Until a functional solution has been developed, you have to "sometimes go astray". Trial and error, reconsideration and further improvements are just as much a part of this process as a lively exchange with a wide variety of people. An open ear for their respective needs is essential in order to create a product that is functional and yet not too complex. Close cooperation with experienced manufacturers is just as important. After all, the product should not only have an appealing, integrable design on paper, on the computer and in the self-built model, but should also be well crafted and manufactured with care. Instead of reinventing the wheel, the tried and tested can be transferred into the present - with an additional benefit that ideally "satisfies everyone". Life will decide whether this succeeds in the best possible way. And therefore you.

Rather, he approaches the solution to such an everyday problem in many small steps, the direction of which is determined by constant observation and questioning. Until a functional solution has been developed, you have to "sometimes go astray". Trial and error, reconsideration and further improvements are just as much a part of this process as a lively exchange with a wide variety of people. An open ear for their respective needs is essential in order to create a product that is functional and yet not too complex. Close cooperation with experienced manufacturers is just as important. After all, the product should not only have an appealing, integrable design on paper, on the computer and in the self-built model, but should also be well crafted and manufactured with care. Instead of reinventing the wheel, the tried and tested can be transferred into the present - with an additional benefit that ideally "satisfies everyone". Life will decide whether this succeeds in the best possible way. And therefore you.

General Information
Evolutionary thrust(-box).
The Ulm Stool - designed in 1955 by Max Bill, the first director of the Ulm University of Design, in collaboration with Hans Gugelot and Paul Hildinger for the students* of this very university - is a furniture as simple as it is multifunctional. It can serve as a seat, a side table, a shelf and a carrying aid for the books needed during studies. It is thus a prime example of the perfection that an object achieves when it can no longer be improved by omission. The variant recently added to it by its Swiss manufacturer - also a design by Master Bill himself - takes away one of these functions, but adds a relevant functional added value in the form of a drawer integrated without fittings.
This drawer, like the stool itself, is made of untreated spruce wood, worked with dovetailed edges and equipped with a simple but effective pull-out stop. Thus, the stool is deprived of its originally intended, but in practice but rather rarely seen functionality as a book carrier, but he fits noticeably better in the role he has grown over the decades as a night and side table.

product_959.description:
General Information
Authentic aesthetics. Stained in color
Three wooden planks that are connected to form a U by finger joints and stabilized on the open side by a round crossbar - the Ulm stool is an impressive example of the art of designing an extremely minimalist and yet multifunctional construction: it can be used as a seat, side table, shelf or carrying aid for books and the like. Designed in the mid-1950s by Max Bill, Bauhaus student, architect and at the time Rector of the Ulm School of Design, in collaboration with Hans Gugelot and Paul Hildinger, the Ulm stool is undisputedly one of the icons of furniture design.
And while its areas of application regularly open up new perspectives, the Ulm Stool itself is also being given a new look. While the original was made from untreated spruce planks - also available from us in this original material - we are now expanding our range to include a colored version made from birch and beech wood. To achieve an authentic aesthetic, the wood is stained in color, not varnished, so that the grain of the wood can still shine through. The famous solid construction has remained the same, as has the production in Switzerland.

As interior equipment for the CONTAINER DS, CONTAINER DS AIR, CONTAINER DS with lock, CONTAINER DS KLEIN we recommend the drawer or the shelf.
Series Container DS
Synonymous with storage and transport: the container in its archetypal surface of folded steel. We offer this cabinet furniture in the miniaturized form of overseas containers in four different versions. These well-proportioned storage boxes serve many purposes and areas of use. All containers have perforations in the bottoms for passing cables. The classic container as well as the flat and small container have doors hinged to the top of the body, which slide into the top of the body when opened and thus almost completely disappear. The CONTAINER DS PLUS is upright and has a conventional hinged door on the side.
The classic: The CONTAINER DS in the proportion of a sea container is virtually the archetype of the series CONTAINER DS. It serves as a cabinet in the living room for china and utensils for the set table, in the office for storing files in standardized format or for paper and office utensils. As a chest of drawers for linen and as a piece of furniture in the hallway and wardrobe. It can be combined in its basic rectangular shape with a variety of complementary accessories. Various feet and casters or the two framework frames serve as the basis. The shelf element TARA has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery. The coat rack completes the container to a functional wardrobe. The container of this format is available in limited color selection equipped with a lock. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The flat one: CONTAINER DS FLAT has the footprint of the classic CONTAINER DS and can be connected to it in height and stacked. It can be combined with the above mentioned accessories of the classic CONTAINER DS. This container often serves as a flat element that is built into a stack of the classic container. It is useful with its special volume for the stack of paper, for utensils and as a shelf for many purposes. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The small one: The CONTAINER DS KLEIN as the little brother of the CONTAINER DS does not have the proportions of a sea container, unlike its archetypal big role model - it is narrower, with identical depth and height. With its small size and unusual formatting, it serves as a piece of side furniture next to the bed and sofa and can also be stacked up to form a tower. It can be equipped with all separate feet as well as the casters. Unlike its sister models, it is always equipped with a smooth cover shelf in the respective color. The shelf element TARA KLEIN has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery.
The big one: A very special piece of furniture with its own range of uses is the CONTAINER DS PLUS. It can be used in portrait format and serves as a locker-like clothes or wardrobe cabinet and can also be used as a large-volume cabinet, individually or stacked on top of each other in the kitchen, office or other places. This large container is stackable like all other sister models via included square connectors. A clothes rail is included, and a specially designed shelf and cover shelf are available separately as accessories.
