General Information
The INOX shelving system was developed as a storage system for sterile goods and sterile clothing and is used as such in laboratories and other sterile rooms. These mesh baskets, which are part of the system, offer plenty of space for all kinds of storage items and can be hooked into the associated wall rails without tools. Whether towels in the bathroom, crockery in the kitchen or scarves and cycle helmets in the checkroom: the mesh baskets provide a well-ventilated and visible place for everything. The baskets are made of high-quality, electrolytically polished stainless steel round material from the medical sector, are virtually indestructible and easy to clean. The carrying handle on the front ensures easy handling and the shape of the frame makes the baskets stackable.
HUPFER - Münsterland efficiency
For 155 years, Hupfer Metallwerke from Coesfeld has been ensuring smooth processes in places where cleanliness is paramount. Founded in 1870 in Saxony-Anhalt as a wire mesh manufacturer, the company equips commercial kitchens, clinics and clean rooms for pharmaceutical companies with its systems. Furniture, trolleys, shelving systems, work surfaces, technology and accessories. With a high degree of specialization, virtually indestructible and ideally adapted to their tasks. The focus here is on special requirements: all Hupfer products must meet special hygiene specifications. This is achieved with a special steel that the company polishes electrolytically, making its surface infinitely durable. The design, in turn, ensures smooth, low-contact processes and high utility value. We have selected a wall hook rail from the medical sector from the wide range on offer, into which various accessories - baskets, hook rails, shelves, etc. - can be hung, and which can thus be combined to create individual storage furniture.

This enables the manufactory to deliver only flawless, tested items, to implement in-house developments directly on site and to fulfill individual customer requests. This results in products that are beyond reproach in terms of quality and workmanship.

Whether you opt for the classic shiny chrome-plated finish or the robust powder-coated finish per se: You can be sure that these things will last. Above all, they will not rust. They are manufactured in Germany, France, Spain and Italy - with a copper content of approx. 58 percent (± 1%).

product_995.product_name: Hinged drawer container, sheet steel, 5-compartment Polychrom Dario
product_995.alt_text: Hinged drawer container, sheet steel, 5-compartment Polychrom Dario
product_995.description:
General Information
Exclusive
We appreciate the good things, and sometimes we want to make the good things a little better. To make the sheet steel pivot container known as the "Pivot Cabinet" accessible to lively room concepts, we have combined fresh colors based on the RAL palette to create a powerful design element of its own. The color combination of the "Dario" container with RAL 2021 water blue and RAL 6027 light green as well as RAL 2012 salmon orange and RAL 3000 fire red around the central RAL 280-2 is available exclusively from Manufactum.
Home Smart Home. Container with a future
Its design is reminiscent of the utopias of the 1960s, its construction has reached maturity, its choice of materials is more sophisticated than ever before and its functionality is as flexible as visionaries could wish for.
Called a "pivot cabinet" in English - "pivot" means something like "pivot joint" or "swivel axis" - this name refers to the essential design element of the container: the individual drawers are swung open on an axis, not pulled open or folded down as is usually the case. This design idea was made famous by Joe Colombo's "Boby" roll container developed in 1970. The Italian architect was also one of the leading futuristic industrial designers of the 1960s, a time of optimism and visions of the future, which - following Herbert Marcuse's train of thought, for example - sought to pave the way out of the realm of necessity and into the realm of freedom. Designs such as Verner Panton's cantilever "Panton Chair", Olivier Mourgue's "Djinn" armchair, which adorned the interior of the space station in "2001 - A Space Odyssey", and Colombo's "Tube Chair" became icons. Colombo's "dynamic pieces of furniture" always aimed to be multifunctional.
Our swivel drawer container builds on the ideal of those designs, but doesn't just quote the utopias of past decades, but smartly brings the future into your home today. While Colombo and his colleagues were still enthusiastic about the newly developed plastics of the 1960s, we know better today and prefer sheet steel, which offers far greater stability and durability. The sheet steel thus reinforces the versatility of the container. In the kitchen, bathroom, living room or entrance area - sturdy and stable, the hinged drawer container takes on its intended functions of storage, presentation and easy access in any environment and, like any successful design object, fulfills the role of eye-catcher in a stylish and colourful way.
Unique color combination: Dario
This vibrant combination of colors is available exclusively from Manufactum. Similar to a color wheel, it completes the arc from blue to red: at the center of the color combination is RAL 280-2, a rather soft and calm color from the RAL Effect spectrum, which mediates between the powerful hues of the upper and lower rotary drawers. Water blue and light green form the fresh, lively upper entry, while warm salmon orange and intense fire red set the lower accent.
With an undivided surface area of around A4 size, the revolving drawers can hold larger and smaller good things. The design is well thought out and solidly constructed: The front round steel, which connects the top cover and base of the container, forms the pivot axis so that the drawers are flush with the rear steel tubes when closed; with the help of a small magnet on the rear wall, they dock into place with a gentle snap. And even if they don't beep or flash to let you know that the fridge needs to be refilled, the drawers reveal all the necessary and possible contents by swiveling open 270 degrees and providing a complete overview. At the bottom, the height-adjustable feet ensure that you can counteract any unevenness in the surface. And if you also want to make your designer furniture more mobile, we offer a separate set of matching castor feet for the swivel drawer container, which you can screw into place of the feet in no time at all.
Attention:
Please observe the maximum permissible load capacity of the revolving drawers. Distribute the weight evenly. Heavier objects should be placed in the lower, lighter ones in the upper revolving drawers. Do not open more than one revolving drawer at a time to avoid tipping over. Do not leave small children unattended with this piece of furniture.

Wall Shelf RM3
A fine wall shelf for books, in the private office as well as the kitchen and bathroom. The RM3 displays perfect material economy – a base made of sheet steel, brackets made of stainless steel and a solid wood profile – these three materials are brought together perfectly in this product. The design is based on the clever use of the respective properties of the three materials. The ends of the shelf supports, made of stainless steel wire and bent several times to the perfect form, engage with the wooden wall profile, connecting the vertical profile and the horizontal shelf with minimal use of material. The basic RM3 shelving unit consists of two wall profiles made of solid ash wood, three shelves with a depth of 20 centimetres as well as the necessary materials for assembly. Additionally, we offer bookends made of stainless steel wire and single-packaged shelves in two depths (besides the regular-sized shelves, shelves with a depth of 30 centimetres fit into the RM3 as well) if you want to upgrade your furniture. The combination of two RM3s on top of each other results in a room-high shelving unit. The wooden profiles feature ends that are cut at an angle that helps them nestling perfectly into each other. The maximum load capacity of a shelf is 15 kilograms.

Container Henry
A shelving tower with multiple uses: HENRY in small, medium and large is an object-like focal point in the room or discreet furniture. HENRY stands freely, independently and accessible from all sides as a room divider or as a complementary piece of furniture in the bathroom, living room or hallway. We strive for this variety of applications in all our MAGAZIN products. In addition to its functionality, this small piece of furniture impresses with its ingenious design: panels milled at a 45-degree angle interlock at different heights. This gives HENRY a very fine contour and at the same time emphasizes the high-quality material, whose plywood core is thus visible. HENRY comes fully assembled. We discovered HENRY and the designers from Studio Sergeant, led by the young Belgian Pieter van den Poel, at an exhibition of graduates from the "Thomas More Hogeschool Mechelen". With the name of their piece of furniture, the young designers want to commemorate the architect Henry van der Velde, who left his home town of Ghent a striking book tower with the architecture of the "Boekentoren" library building.

product_1007.description:
General Information
Discover MAGAZIN products: Collaborating with innovative designers, MAGAZIN develops and produces this unique furniture and home accessories series.
Like a tray, this top made of sheet steel sits as a top closure on the CONTAINER DS, CONTAINER DS AIR, CONTAINER DS with lock, CONTAINER DS FLAT or the TARA shelf element. The recesses at the four corners hold the top positively on the respective substructure. A practical addition as a shelf in the office, living room or entrance area and for many other purposes.
Series Container DS
Synonymous with storage and transport: the container in its archetypal surface of folded steel. We offer this cabinet furniture in the miniaturized form of overseas containers in four different versions. These well-proportioned storage boxes serve many purposes and areas of use. All containers have perforations in the bottoms for passing cables. The classic container as well as the flat and small container have doors hinged to the top of the body, which slide into the top of the body when opened and thus almost completely disappear. The CONTAINER DS PLUS is upright and has a conventional hinged door on the side.
The classic: The CONTAINER DS in the proportion of a sea container is virtually the archetype of the series CONTAINER DS. It serves as a cabinet in the living room for china and utensils for the set table, in the office for storing files in standardized format or for paper and office utensils. As a chest of drawers for linen and as a piece of furniture in the hallway and wardrobe. It can be combined in its basic rectangular shape with a variety of complementary accessories. Various feet and casters or the two framework frames serve as the basis. The shelf element TARA has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery. The coat rack completes the container to a functional wardrobe. The container of this format is available in limited color selection equipped with a lock. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The flat one: CONTAINER DS FLAT has the footprint of the classic CONTAINER DS and can be connected to it in height and stacked. It can be combined with the above mentioned accessories of the classic CONTAINER DS. This container often serves as a flat element that is built into a stack of the classic container. It is useful with its special volume for the stack of paper, for utensils and as a shelf for many purposes. It can be mounted on the wall with a separately available bracket.
The small one: The CONTAINER DS KLEIN as the little brother of the CONTAINER DS does not have the proportions of a sea container, unlike its archetypal big role model - it is narrower, with identical depth and height. With its small size and unusual formatting, it serves as a piece of side furniture next to the bed and sofa and can also be stacked up to form a tower. It can be equipped with all separate feet as well as the casters. Unlike its sister models, it is always equipped with a smooth cover shelf in the respective color. The shelf element TARA KLEIN has the outer contour of the container and can be stacked with it in height via connectors included in the delivery.
The big one: A very special piece of furniture with its own range of uses is the CONTAINER DS PLUS. It can be used in portrait format and serves as a locker-like clothes or wardrobe cabinet and can also be used as a large-volume cabinet, individually or stacked on top of each other in the kitchen, office or other places. This large container is stackable like all other sister models via included square connectors. A clothes rail is included, and a specially designed shelf and cover shelf are available separately as accessories.

product_1008.product_name: Hook rail for Inox shelving system
product_1008.alt_text: Hook rail for Inox shelving system
product_1008.description:
General Information
The INOX shelving system was developed as a storage system for sterile goods and sterile clothing and is used as such in laboratories and other sterile rooms. Medical staff hang their shoes on this hook rail for the INOX shelving system after work. We quickly repurpose them and bring them, together with wall rails and other accessories, into the living area as storage furniture. They can be hooked into the corresponding wall rails without tools and used as towel rails in the bathroom, as shoe or bag holders in the checkroom or as cooking utensil holders in the kitchen. Made of electrolytically polished and burr-free stainless steel wire, the hooks are virtually indestructible and easy to clean. Incidentally, the hook rail can also be screwed to the wall without the accompanying wall rails and used as a shoe rack. The fixing material required for this application is not included in the scope of delivery.
HUPFER - Münsterland efficiency
For 155 years, Hupfer Metallwerke from Coesfeld has been ensuring smooth processes in places where cleanliness is paramount. Founded in 1870 in Saxony-Anhalt as a wire mesh manufacturer, the company equips commercial kitchens, clinics and clean rooms for pharmaceutical companies with its systems. Furniture, trolleys, shelving systems, work surfaces, technology and accessories. With a high degree of specialization, virtually indestructible and ideally adapted to their tasks. The focus here is on special requirements: all Hupfer products must meet special hygiene specifications. This is achieved with a special steel that the company polishes electrolytically, making its surface infinitely durable. The design, in turn, ensures smooth, low-contact processes and high utility value. We have selected a wall hook rail from the medical sector from the wide range on offer, into which various accessories - baskets, hook rails, shelves, etc. - can be hung, and which can thus be combined to create individual storage furniture.

product_1016.description:
General Information
Viewed as a whole
In addition to its simple, straightforward design, this wall mirror is characterized by the accurate, solid craftsmanship typical of "Form & Refine": the solid oak slats are dowelled, glued and finally oiled in carpentry style. Above all, however, the wall mirror has a significant functional advantage: it is considerably higher than a conventional wall mirror and therefore offers the possibility of holistic viewing. If you mount the mirror firmly on the wall - with the involvement of any roommates - small people will be able to see more than just the top of their head, while tall people are no longer limited to the reflection of their décolleté. And a little distance is rewarded by a view that can be inspected from head to toe - especially as it seems advisable, especially in times of working from home, to quickly check before leaving the house whether the sock color matches or whether the jogging bottoms have been swapped for jeans. Incidentally, the wall mirror is not only exceptionally high, but also somewhat narrower than many of its colleagues, which means it can be installed in some niches, for example next to the front door...
Form & Refine. Danish design
Form & Refine is a Danish design label founded in 2018 by Helle Herman Mortensen, Jonas Herman Pedersen and Lasse Lund Lauridsen. It exemplarily follows the Scandinavian design tradition and continues it at the same time. A central point is the harmonious combination of aesthetics, function and material. The designs are clear and restrained, function leads to form and the pure materials, which are allowed to retain their original visual details and forms, are processed with perfect craftsmanship. This is always done in the countries of origin of the materials, which shortens transport distances and at the same time supports the local craft culture.
Responsible economic operator for the EU

product_1020.description:
General Information
A Twofold Advantage: Mounted to the Wall, Still Ready at Hand. Plus, Made of Optical Glass.
This mirror comes with a sturdy concertina arm and a frame made from solid, durably chrome-plated brass. The mirror glass consists of a material rarely used for this purpose: optical glass. The manufacturing process of optical glass is rather tricky, and producing the convex shape requires a multi-step routine. Usually, you find optical glass in the form of lenses in loupes and cameras. Lensmakers have to pay a good deal more attention to the purity of the glass when the magnification rates are higher; therefore, they have to reduce air inclusions and impurities to an absolute minimum.
A concertina arm holds this mirror in place just so that you can adjust the reflection to your needs or you can take the mirror in your hand eventually and put it back into its holder afterwards. One side of this mirror simply reflects the image of whatever is in front of it; the other side magnifies the image five times. The manufacturer Windisch, a family business in Barcelona, has specialized in the handcrafted production of mirrors and bathroom utensils made of brass since its foundation in 1934.

Wall arm and bezel in chrome-plated brass. Mirror made of optical glass. One side normal mirror view, other side five times magnifying. Height 37 cm, Ø including frame 18,5 cm. Projection 12,5-62 cm. Weight 1.5 kg. Supplied with mounting hardware.

product_1022.product_name: Stand spotlight Wittenberg, Deep black RAL 9005
product_1022.alt_text: Stand spotlight Wittenberg, Deep black RAL 9005
product_1022.description:
General Information
In this model, the ceiling- and wall-mounted spotlight WITTENBERG becomes a luminaire that you can position on any ground. The spotlight type DRUFF performs its service wherever you need accent lighting from below or when there is no power supply via wall or ceiling outlets. DRUFF may stand on the floor, on top of a sideboard, or a shelf. WITTENBERG 4.0 features an intricate, beautifully crafted housing that dispenses with visible screws or cables. The spotlight heads sit slightly recessed in the rectangular housing; nevertheless, you can rotate them 365 degrees and tilt them 90 degrees. When maintenance tasks are required, a patented bayonet catch enables you to detach the entire light head from the housing in the blink of an eye. The light emission angle of the lamps is 12 degrees, providing focused light. We have two attachment lenses included in the delivery. These lenses create a light output of 38 degrees and give off a wide beam. Cable: L 250 cm, safety plug (type F). The luminaire contains LED lamps. Luminous flux: 1,100 lm, colour temperature: 2,700 K, colour rendering index (CRI > 90), wattage rating: 2 × 12.7 W. Swappable optics: beam angle 12° and 38°.
wittenberg 4.0 - the all-rounder
The variety and flexibility of the wittenberg system luminaire family is unsurpassed. wittenberg 4.0 is the most versatile system luminaire from mawa and is very often used in customized applications. With the fourth generation of the multifunctional light head, the entire luminaire series has been technically enhanced and formally reduced to what is possible. Future compatibility and a conscious use of resources are particularly important to mawa.
mawa
The brand identity of mawa, the luminaire manufacturer based on the outskirts of Berlin, comprises producing luminaires and lighting systems with innovative technologies and resourceful manufacturing processes. Designs that promise longevity are the main focus of mawa’s development and design department. One of the manufacturer’s primary concerns is to keep the consumption of resources in the production of luminaires in balance. From the first sketches to the prototypes ready for series production, luminaires by mawa are unique originals. Awarded with many design prizes, they grace museum collections all over the world. The brand’s small crew – with lighting enthusiast, founder, and doyen Martin Wallroth at the centre – has been a force to be reckoned with in the industry for years. They excelled in luminaire development (as represented in our range) as well as in lighting design for exhibitions, museums and trade fair stands. In all areas, mawa products are convincing in terms of design, material, finish, details, and lighting technology.

product_1030.description:
General Information
The task light from the AYNO luminaire range is primarily designed as table lighting. Version 2.0 has an updated, flicker-free lighting technology, excellent color rendering, the LED has a service life of 50,000 hours.

The luminaire contains LED lamps. Nominal wattage: 13 watts, light temperature: 2,700 Kelvin, luminous flux: 1,506 lumens, color rendering RA95. Cable: L 105 cm - from the dimmer. Euro plug (type C).
AYNO luminaires
With the AYNO luminaire family, industrial designer Stefan Diez has created a new, contemporary type of luminaire typology, bridging the gap between the origins and the present of steerable light. AYNO is quite radically reduced to the essentials and meets all requirements in terms of design, contemporary technology and resource conservation.

The central feature of the AYNO luminaire family is a fiberglass rod that is formed into an arc by the luminaire cable. The inherent tension of the rod enables a joint-free design. By moving the two adjustment rings on the base and head, the fiberglass rod is bent into the desired position and the light is directed in the required direction. The cable thus stretches the rod into an arc, the radius of which can be varied as required using the adjustment rings. The fine adjustment, i.e. ultimately the exact alignment of the light, is achieved with the adjustable lampshade.

AYNO reflects a radical approach to circular design. An essential step here is the reduction of structures and complexity. The resulting minimalist construction enables extremely low resource consumption. The luminaire consists of only three fully recyclable primary materials: steel, glass fiber and ABS plastic. The steel and plastic elements are already made from recycled materials. In addition, the design means that all materials can be separated by type and thus recycled. No tools are required to achieve this - everything is interlocked and can be separated by hand. Access to so-called semi-finished products, i.e. materials and elements pre-produced as standard in large series, reduces costs and shortens transportation routes. The luminaire is durable as it can be repaired by the user without tools. And even the luminaire head, the LED unit produced in Germany or the transformer can be easily replaced.

AYNO is available in our online store as a table or floor luminaire. A larger floor and wall lamp can also be ordered in our stores. Our staff will be happy to assist you with your selection.

product_1032.description:
General Information
The popular SONNENGLAS® in a small version: the glass of this variant holds 250 ml. The principle of this solar lamp is as simple as it is ingenious: during the day, the highly efficient solar and light module integrated into the lid of the glass container stores solar energy, which can be used for lighting in the dark. Ideal as atmospheric lighting on an outdoor dining table, windowsill or balcony parapet. This technically enhanced version has an additional switch, a colored charge level indicator, is also dimmable and splash-proof. The glass container under the light unit provides distance from the illuminated surface, can be filled decoratively and creates a small island of light that can even be used as a reading light in the immediate vicinity. A small bracket on the screw cap serves as a magnetic switch. When this is activated, the light switches on and off automatically from a certain level of illuminance, for example at sunrise and sunset. The integrated sun module is also fully functional without the glass container and can be used as a mobile light. It can be switched on and off using the control button and also has an emergency light function in which the LEDs flash. SONNENGLAS® is produced in a fair trade project in South Africa and enjoys a cult following there. For additional charging of the batteries, there is a USB-C connection in the light unit (the charging cable is not included) with fast charging: 10 hours of light duration after just 10 minutes of charging. Protection class: IP64. Lighting duration up to 100 hours after each full charge. Technical data of the six built-in LEDs: Luminous flux: Infinitely dimmable between 5 and 100 lumens, color temperature: 3,000 K (soft, warm, flicker-free light), service life: 25,000 h, rated output: 120 mW. 1 × solar module (3 V, 135 mA) and 1 × lithium-ion battery (3.7 V, 600 mAh) are included in the scope of delivery. The light contains LED lamps and a lithium-ion battery.

product_1035.description:
General Information
Wood and Glass. The Cesta.
Cesta (basket) is the name of this versatile lamp. You find its origin neither in Japan nor Scandinavia but in Barcelona. The icon of contemporary Catalan design, Miguel Milá, designed it as early as 1962, and since 1996 it has been manufactured by Santa & Cole in Barcelona. With a self-conception like a publishing house, the busy company is always on the lookout for rare pieces of 20th-century craft and industrial culture – the floor lamp “Pie de Salón” is another example in our range. It is a stroke of luck that Santa & Cole, in collaboration with Milá, gave the Cesta an evolutionary boost before reissuing it. The original rattan frame is now made of steam-bent cherry wood, and the shade – still featuring circular cut-outs at the top and bottom – is made of single-layer etched glass instead of plastic. The swivelling handle makes it easy to move the lamp from A to B – from table to floor, for example. You can even use it on balconies and terraces as long as the weather is dry. In any case, thanks to its dimmer switch, it provides a soft to veritable, perfectly homogeneous and glare-free light.

product_1036.description:
General Information
Not the lamp. The light
"It is not from the chair but from sitting, not from the glass but from drinking, not from the jug but from holding and pouring. Not from the lamp, but from the light and glow." Wilhelm Wagenfeld, whose work was honored with an exhibition in Bremen in 2010 on the occasion of his 110th birthday, was the "industrial designer" of his time par excellence and, alongside Peter Behrens, the founding father of a profession in Germany that is represented in almost every major manufacturing company today. However, he himself struggled with the term, even rejecting it. For him, "design" meant that the designed object threatened to be original, possibly even expressing the individuality of a designer's personality, and nothing was further from his mind than that. In 1924, in the Bauhaus metal workshop under the direction of Moholy-Nagy, he created one of his most famous designs, the Bauhaus table lamp. Like his time at the Bauhaus, it was formative for his thinking, even if he would later attest to the lamp's questionable proximity to handicrafts - not in terms of technology and design, which he considered successful throughout his life, but because of the Bauhaus's distance from industry: the lamp was not a mass product and could never become one.

product_1038.alt_text: Guidelight universal light, RAL 1004 Golden yellow
product_1038.description:
General Information
GUIDELIGHT is either a small spotlight or atmospheric all-round light, because depending on how the spherical luminaire head is turned, it casts a focused, direct light or illuminates the elegant luminaire body. The warm white LEDs are powered by an integrated rechargeable battery, making the compact luminaire suitable for use anywhere - it can be easily transported on the metal bracket or hung from a branch or hook. The light can be dimmed continuously using the rotary knob on the side of the light head. The USB-C connection for the charging cable (not included) is located on the opposite side. Fully charged and at maximum light intensity, GUIDELIGHT provides light for up to 5 hours; at lower light intensity, the battery lasts up to 100 hours. GUIDELIGHT is splash-proof and therefore suitable for outdoor use, but should remain indoors during heavy rainfall. Luminous flux: 190 lm, color temperature: 2,700-2,900 K, rated power: 3 W. Protection class IP42. The luminaire contains LED lamps.
Weltevree®
Floris Schoonderbeek and Dick van Hoff founded the label WELTEVREE® in 2007 in Arnhem, the Netherlands. The two designers transfer original and, at the same time, wonderfully simple ideas into excellent craftsmanship. They cooperate closely with experienced producers and suppliers and have authentic products created in their workshops that show one thing outright: Their design derives directly from life – not from an image on a computer screen. The functionality of WELTEVREE®’s products is evident at first sight. One doesn’t need to be a design expert to imagine how nice it is to cook outdoors, relax in a wood-heated bath anywhere or roll a bench effortlessly from one place to another. WELTEVREE® is modern and innovative, yet at the same time ironic and totally unimpressed by current design trends. The label combines unorthodox design solutions with traditional craftsmanship and solid materials. The manufacturers understand functionality and quality as the basis for feeling comfortable, after all. Besides, the old Dutch word “weltevree”, indeed, means “very satisfied”.

Mobile rechargeable lights are currently omnipresent, not least because they are extremely practical to use and versatile. However, there are also major differences here - in terms of materials, shape and performance. Here comes a luminaire from Grau in Hamburg, which in our opinion currently marks the top end in this segment. It starts with the material. The housing is made of visually and haptically pleasant light grey powder-coated die-cast aluminum, the diffuser is made of sturdy polycarbonate. Then there's the function: the luminaire body has the shape of a cone, which on the one hand provides space for the built-in rechargeable batteries, which give the luminaire a runtime of no less than 8 to 150 hours. On the other hand, it reflects the light into the room at a favorable angle (remember: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection).
The light itself is almost a science in itself. At its brightest level, it emits 450 lumens, which generally leaves marketable alternatives far behind. Above all, however, the light can be switched in three color temperature ranges based on natural daylight: 2,200-2,700 Kelvin, 1,700-2,200 Kelvin and 1,300-1,700 Kelvin. They can be selected and dimmed as required using a touch dimmer in the head of the luminaire (on/off, dimming) and a switch under the base (change of dimming spectrum). This switch can also be used to activate a sleep mode in which the luminaire automatically dims from 2,700 Kelvin to a sunset-like 1,300 Kelvin within 30 minutes and then switches itself off. Such functions are referred to as Human Centric Light (HCL), which describes lighting that is specially designed to optimize the interaction between light and people and thus promote well-being.
The luminaire, which is manufactured in Hamburg, is charged using a USB-C cable (supplied without mains adapter). An LED next to the USB port indicates the current charging status during use. What's practical: defective components or batteries can be replaced at the factory if necessary.

product_1045.description:
General Information
From metal to glass.
Poul Henningsen designed this lamp shade consisting of three sections and presented it at a Paris exhibition in 1925. At the time the shades were still made from metal, but Henningsen soon replaced them with models featuring opal glass shades, in which around 12% of the light were omitted to the outside and therefore with a soft and diffuse light distribution it contributes to room illumination. The interiors of the shade segments are given a matt finish through sandblasting, as a result of which the majority of the light – also non-reflective – is directed downwards. The lamp shade consists of three sections: an upper segment of 28.5 cm diameter and two smaller segments underneath. Symbiotic connection. Poul Henningsen and Louis Poulsen.

The lamps of the Danish manufacturer Louis Poulsen have been a benchmark for decades. They owe their development to the ground-breaking work of Poul Henningsen (1894–1967). After giving up his studies as an architect he began working as a freelancer in the field of functional architecture, he wanted to create lamps which provided completely non-reflective, indirect light and at the same time offered an efficient light yield. He was able to achieve this aim through the cooperative partnership which began with Louis Poulsen in 1925 and lasted until his death. Henningsen performed pioneering work with regard to light structures, shades, reflection and light projection. In short, his work laid the foundation stone of the theory of light with which Louis Poulsen manufactures lamps today.

product_1049.description:
General Information
Not the lamp. The light
"It is not from the chair but from sitting, not from the glass but from drinking, not from the jug but from holding and pouring. Not from the lamp, but from the light and glow." Wilhelm Wagenfeld, whose work was honored with an exhibition in Bremen in 2010 on the occasion of his 110th birthday, was the "industrial designer" of his time par excellence and, alongside Peter Behrens, the founding father of a profession in Germany that is represented in almost every major manufacturing company today. However, he himself struggled with the term, even rejecting it. For him, "design" meant that the designed object threatened to be original, possibly even expressing the individuality of a designer's personality, and nothing was further from his mind than that. In 1924, in the Bauhaus metal workshop under the direction of Moholy-Nagy, he created one of his most famous designs, the Bauhaus table lamp. Like his time at the Bauhaus, it was formative for his thinking, even if he would later attest to the lamp's questionable proximity to handicrafts - not in terms of technology and design, which he considered successful throughout his life, but because of the Bauhaus's distance from industry: the lamp was not a mass product and could never become one.

The TIMES table lamp is a compact and portable luminaire made in northern Italy. The consistent structure of basic geometric shapes gives the luminaire its minimalist character, while its unusual proportions make it appear light and friendly. product_1072.description:
General Information
Shade made of triple flashed glass (triplex glass): a layer of clear glass, above a layer of white and then again a layer of clear glass.
Desk lamp: Banker's Lamp
A so-called banker's lamp: this beautiful piece is manufactured from brass; a 3 kg cast iron insert in the footplate gives it a secure stand. The glass shade, which can be rotated around its longitudinal axis, can be adjusted in height by 23 cm; the lamp is switched on and off by means of a brass pull switch. The lampshades are elaborately mouth-blown and consist of multi-layered flashed glass. The white version has a three-layer structure - one layer of clear glass, above it a layer of white glass and then another layer of clear glass. In the green version, a fourth layer of colored glass is added between the clear glass layers to the white glass layer.
Brass Lights from Berlin.
The Berlin lighting manufacturers had their heyday at the beginning of the 20th century, the imprint of the Art Nouveau style is unmistakable. You will notice how good these lights are at the very moment when you set them up respectively hang them up: The metal parts are made of solid brass or, in the case of long pipes, made of brass plated steel. The lampshades are made of hand-blown glass; they gain their shape in wooden forms. The electrical leads are solid textile cables. The ceiling roses are made of porcelain or brass. The patina dyed brass is not lacquered, so the patina can be partially or entirely removed by careful brushing with fine steel wool to emphasize contours or to heighten the shine. A trace of olive oil, applied with a lint-free cloth, is all the care the brass needs. Unlike the most uninhibitedly historicised replicas, the Berlin brass lights are of timeless clarity.

product_1079.description:
General Information
Hand-Painted Decors.
At BTC’s, an experienced employee decorates the lampshades by hand with the different line patterns. Bowles hired her when her previous employer, a big player in the industry, gave up hand-painting. Since then, Bowles has been making the hand-painted lamps simply because he wants to and his employee can.
Bone China from Great Britain.
Bone china is one of the most precious porcelains in the world. It is shining in white when properly burnt and highly break-proof even when pulled out wafer-thin. The most surprising property of bone china is, by all means, its translucency producing a softly shimmering and warm-white colour when illuminated. Finally, in the middle of the 18th century, a small earthenware factory in Great Britain revealed the requisite secret knowledge for producing bone china, long known only in China. Adding bone ash made it possible to fire translucent porcelain in an earthenware kiln at 1,200 °C. Even today, the intricate mixture of kaolin, feldspar, quartz sand and more than 50% burnt bone ash still limits the mechanization of production – and the number of manufactories worldwide that master the craft. We have found a manufacturer in Great Britain with the required craftsman skills. He masters the formulation of the mixture, firing at different temperatures and the finish for exquisite bone china lamps.
British, in Detail. Lamps from BTC.
Lamps made by BTC (= British Timeless Classics), in the vicinity of Oxford, have attained the status of timeless classics. The creative spirit and driving force behind the firm is Peter Bowles, who pursues his very clear idea and just as clearly realises his agenda. The process starts with the manufacture: Bowles wants to produce lamps that are British down to the level of detail. For example, the bone china-lamp shades come from a pottery in Stoke-on-Trent, known as the "the Potteries" because of the almost 500 potteries that used to be located there. Almost all are gone today and the firm, which also belongs to Bowles, would not exist except for BTC. He took it over when it was on the brink of bankruptcy and has restructured it while keeping all the employees. The hand-blown glass domes come from a glass blowing shop in Worcestershire which Bowles also bought. In addition to domes for lamps, the shop produces coloured glass windows for historical buildings and churches. A handful of glass blowers with their two small smelting furnaces practice the methods of glass blowing and uphold the once famous English tradition of this trade. The British manufacture of the lamps extends to the cables, too. Bowles was dissatisfied with the plastic wrapped cables on his first lamp, so he used a locally produced cloth wrapped cable from a clothes iron for his exhibition piece. The reaction was so positive that he has used cloth cable since. They are locally produced near the firm in home-based work.

product_1080.product_name: Midgard spring table lamp, With stand
product_1080.alt_text: Midgard spring table lamp, With stand
product_1080.description:
General Information
Flexibility through spring balancer
The spring balancer lamp is today's widespread economy edition of the work lamps from the Bauhaus environment. With it the complex joint constructions for the inclination adjustment of well functioning tension springs were replaced economically. It was produced by Midgard in Auma in Thuringia from the 1950s until 2011 - and it was in the Manufactum range for a good ten years.
Now it's back. And as before, this version aligned with the historical original is not to be compared with the cheap replicas, as a look at the details shows: strong, not wearing out tension springs, sturdy 12 mm square steel tubes, a clamp foot made of die-cast aluminum or a stand made of steel, in which the carrier linkage rotates and a neat metal toggle switch on the screen.
Midgard. A Pioneer in Directing Light.
“Better work results, power savings, eye protection – all accounted for by Midgard’s adjustable turn-in lights.” Nothing less than that was the claim that the cover page of an old Midgard catalogue proclaimed full-bodied. Curt Fischer was behind the company founded in 1919 in the Thuringian city Auma. The engineer and designer held the world’s oldest patent for dirigible light and from the very beginning devoted a great deal of attention to every last component of each of his luminaires. In any case, his impulse to renew the traditional resulted in a mutual closeness to and sympathy with the Bauhaus avant-garde. In 1926, Midgard lamps, featuring the aesthetics of precise machines, unsurprisingly, were part of the furnishings of the newly erected Bauhaus building complex in Dessau. Decades later – after the company’s socialisation to “VEB Industrieleuchtenbau Auma” and the reprivatisation in the 1990s – Midgard’s long history ended in 2011 with insolvency. In 2017, however, David Einsiedler and Joke Rasch revived the traditional brand and set up a manufactory in Hamburg-Altona. Since then, production has remained there. And as before, it is still true: All Midgard luminaires are manufactured entirely in Germany.

product_1081.product_name: Tonone desk lamp steel and aluminum 2 arms, With base
product_1081.alt_text: Tonone desk lamp steel and aluminum 2 arms, With base
product_1081.description:
General Information
Tonone lamp series.
Two-arm desk lamp based on the principle of mechanical construction: TONONE lamps possess an industrial appearance and consist of precisely worked components with a finely-structured, powder-coated surface. The simplicity of construction is impressive because omitting certain components, the simplification of detail and construction makes – as is often the case – a product which is both popular and accessible. A convincing lamp series, to a certain extent of radical and archaic simplicity, which also functions well, which is in line with requirements and without multidimensional joints or a sensory light control system. The construction is securely positioned on a cast iron base, has two perforated plates, enclosed ball bearings and joints with steel spring, which are opened and closed with a small tool for adjustment which is included in the delivery. The series includes the one or two-arm work or desk lamp with clamp or base, a floor lamp and a wall lamp with a shade which can be swivelled to the side and one with a rigid shade. All lamps belonging to the TONONE family (apart from the wall lamp with the rigid shade) are turned on and off via a push switch on the lamp shade.
Tonone luminaires. Exemplary industrial design
The clever modular concept for Tonone luminaires comes from the Netherlands. The designing mind behind it is Anton de Groof, who is neither a designer nor an engineer, but enthusiastic about traditional mechanics and technology. Consequently, the design language of the lamps is that of a mechanical construction that does justice to the industrial manufacturing process and combines simplicity with spirit in a thoughtful way - which places them formally in the environment of Bauhaus and Werkbund. It is noteworthy that the lights are not only mature, but also economically keep the all too rarely realized promise of industrial design to deliver technically as well as aesthetically high quality products at affordable prices.
All models in the series are built from always recurring identical parts. This starts with the heavy cast iron base, made in Belgium, and extends to the steel arm segments, which, like the aluminum shade, are covered with a highly reflective powder coating. Each joint is multiply adjustable thanks to five steel balls between two perforated discs with 23 holes - but only at angles that won't pinch your fingers or cause the lamp to tip. The enclosed adjustment key is reminiscent of old industrial luminaires. Tonone luminaires are switched by a push switch located just outside the shade on the socket. The lampshades are open at the top and bottom, which allows them to shine downward light on a surface to be illuminated and upward to contribute to indirect room lighting.
Purist. The Bolt series
Puristic, clear and functional are the lights of the series Bolt. All models consist of recurring, identical parts. This begins with the heavy cast iron base, manufactured in Belgium, and extends to the steel arm segments, which, like the aluminum lampshade, are covered with a highly reflective powder coating. Each joint is multiply adjustable thanks to five steel balls between two perforated discs with 23 holes - but only at angles that won't pinch your fingers or cause the lamp to tip. The included adjustment key is reminiscent of old industrial luminaires. The lampshades are open at the top and bottom, so they cast downward light onto the surface to be illuminated and contribute upward to indirect room lighting. The Bolt series is switched by a push switch located just outside the shade on the socket.
